issues.title: Remove unused window-resizing and string-escaping Objective-C categories
issues.evidence: Repo/XIB/dynamic-reference search and released symbols
issues.body:
Type: maintenance / redundant code. Priority: low. Confidence: high for no current callers in this application.

Audited version: 2.1.8 (build 160), main commit `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`, local macOS 27.0.1 / Xcode 27. This issue records future work; no implementation was changed during the audit.

## Evidence

The following categories are still compiled and linked into the distributed app but have no external callers in tracked application sources, tests, XIBs, property lists, or third-party text sources:

- [AKNSWindow+Resizing.m:24–33](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKNSWindow%2BResizing.m#L24): `ak_resizeForContentViewSize:animate:`.
- [AKNSString+Escaping.m:24–47](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKNSString%2BEscaping.m#L24): `ak_escapeFirstCharacterFromString:`, `ak_escapeQuotes`, and `ak_escapeParentheses`. The first method is referenced only by the two wrappers in its own category.

The resizing header remains imported by [CallController](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallController.m#L25), [ActiveCallViewController](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/ActiveCallViewController.m#L22), and [CallTransferController](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallTransferController.m#L21), although none invokes the category.

Both implementation files remain in the Telephone target's [Sources phase](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj#L3730). Symbol inspection of the exact released 2.1.8 executable confirmed all four method implementations and the category metadata remain linked. Repository-wide selector searches found no nib action, dynamic selector string, or external invocation. Categories that are actively used, including AddressBook querying/localisation and NSString PJSUA/scanning, were excluded.

## Why clean this up

These helpers add unused code and misleading imports to the current compact-window implementation. The old resizing helper replaces the entire content view, so retaining it also risks accidental reuse that discards controls. This is a maintenance finding, not a currently reachable window bug or a claim of measurable performance gain.

## Proposed future change

Remove the two unused categories, their target/file references, and the three stale resizing imports. Confirm all supported build configurations and Objective-C/Swift bridging paths still compile. Keep the current window layout and call/SIP behaviour intact. If future resizing is needed, use the current controller layout code and AppKit's documented [setContentSize(_:) API](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nswindow/setcontentsize(_:)) while preserving the content hierarchy.

## Acceptance checks

- Build Debug and Release locally; check target membership and bridging imports.
- Re-run native Settings open/switch/close tests and all call/transfer state transitions.
- Verify keyboard controls, focus, and compact window sizing.
- Confirm these category symbols are absent from the resulting executable.
- Recheck selector references before deletion; this audit did not inspect private third-party plug-ins or future consumers.

issues.title: Preserve existing call history when loading its file fails
issues.evidence: Scratch-file read denial through actual history/storage code
issues.body:
Type: backend bug. Priority: P2. Confidence: high.

Affected: jps Telephone 2.1.8 (build 160), macOS 27.0.1 / Xcode 27. Audited main commit `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`. This is future work; source and the published build were left unchanged.

## Trigger and observed behaviour

A valid account history file is temporarily unreadable while its parent directory remains writable, for example after a permissions/ACL or file-provider problem. The next completed call adds a record.

SimplePropertyListStorage.load throws the read error. PersistentCallHistory.init catches it and retains an empty origin without a failed-load state. add then saves that empty origin plus the new record; Foundation atomic write replaces the existing file.

All prior saved records for that account can be permanently replaced with the new record. Atomic writes protect against partial writes but do not protect history that was never successfully loaded.

## Source evidence

- [UseCases/PersistentCallHistory.swift:33–38](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/UseCases/PersistentCallHistory.swift#L33-L38)
- [UseCases/PersistentCallHistory.swift:47–49](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/UseCases/PersistentCallHistory.swift#L47-L49)
- [Telephone/SimplePropertyListStorage.swift:33–44](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/SimplePropertyListStorage.swift#L33-L44)

## Local reproduction

Run history-read-failure.swift compiled with current Telephone/SimplePropertyListStorage.swift and the 9a32 local Release UseCases/Domain frameworks. It writes two real production history records in a private temporary directory, sets only that test file to mode0200, observes NSCocoaError257, initializes the production wrapper, adds a third record, restores test-file readability and observes exactly one new record on disk. Fixture removes its own temporary files.

Validation: runtime validated against actual production storage source and exact Release UseCases framework. The isolated harness and log are retained locally under `outputs/audit-2.1.8/backend/`; the reproduction uses synthetic `audit.invalid` records. No user data is required.

## Future fix and regression checks

Distinguish absent file from unsuccessful load. Keep failed-load state and refuse destructive persistence until a successful retry/recovery or explicit user-approved reset; surface the failure and preserve the existing bytes.

Use valid on-disk history with read denied and parent writable; assert add cannot replace prior bytes after failed load. Restore permissions, retry, then assert old and new records are preserved. Also test malformed data and genuinely nonexistent file separately.

Existing coverage gap: PersistentCallHistoryTests covers successful add/remove/removeAll using memory storage; it has no read-error state followed by a later write.

## Apple documentation and limits

- [NSData.WritingOptions.atomic](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/nsdata/writingoptions/atomic): Atomic writing writes an auxiliary file and replaces the original after success.

No real profile, SIP, file-provider or UI was accessed. This proves permission-denial data loss, not the frequency of such errors on user devices.

issues.title: Do not report Clear History as complete when deleting its file fails
issues.evidence: Scratch-file delete denial and subsequent reload
issues.body:
Type: backend bug. Priority: P2. Confidence: high.

Affected: jps Telephone 2.1.8 (build 160), macOS 27.0.1 / Xcode 27. Audited main commit `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`. This is future work; source and the published build were left unchanged.

## Trigger and observed behaviour

A person selects Clear History while the account history file cannot be removed, for example a read-only/permission-denied containing directory.

PersistentCallHistory.removeAll clears the in-memory origin before storage.delete. Deletion failure is caught and printed, without restoring records or returning an error. The current history appears empty while the on-disk history remains.

The supposedly deleted call history is retained and reappears when the account/app reloads; this breaks both persistence and the user expectation that Clear History deleted the record.

## Source evidence

- [UseCases/PersistentCallHistory.swift:57–63](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/UseCases/PersistentCallHistory.swift#L57-L63)
- [Telephone/SimplePropertyListStorage.swift:47–52](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/SimplePropertyListStorage.swift#L47-L52)

## Local reproduction

The second case in history-read-failure.swift creates a production record in a private directory, sets only that directory to mode0500, calls actual removeAll, observes NSCocoaError513 and empty in-memory history, constructs a new wrapper and observes the old record restored. Permissions are reset and test data removed.

Validation: runtime validated against actual production storage source and exact Release UseCases framework. The isolated harness and log are retained locally under `outputs/audit-2.1.8/backend/`; the reproduction uses synthetic `audit.invalid` records. No user data is required.

## Future fix and regression checks

Make clearing transactional: propagate deletion failure and keep/restore the displayed records until durable deletion succeeds. Display an actionable failure rather than signalling completion through an empty list.

Inject delete failure or deny writes on a scratch parent directory; assert UI/use-case error and unchanged history. A successful retry must remove the file and keep the history empty after reload.

Existing coverage gap: Existing tests assert that delete is called and memory storage becomes empty, but have no throwing storage or restart-after-failed-delete check.

## Apple documentation and limits

- [FileManager.removeItem(at:)](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/filemanager/removeitem(at:)): Deletion is a throwing operation; a failure does not mean the item was removed.

Only isolated file permissions and non-UI history objects were exercised; no real history was read or cleared.

issues.title: Active-call dead-key input raises an out-of-bounds exception
issues.evidence: Exact native handler with an empty dead-key event
issues.body:
Type: validated correctness bug. Priority: P2 / medium. Confidence: High: reproduced in exact compiled production view.

Affected: jps Telephone 2.1.8 (build 160), local macOS 27.0.1 / Xcode 27. Audited commit `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`. No production code or published build was changed during this audit.

## Trigger and observed behaviour

With an active call card receiving keyboard input, press a dead-key combination such as Option-E. Apple documents an empty NSEvent.characters string for this event.

AKActiveCallView.keyDown indexes characters at position0 without checking length. The exact native production method raises NSInvalidArgumentException before forwarding the event.

Ordinary keyboard input interrupts event processing during a call. Process termination and call disconnection are not established; AppKit may contain the event exception.

## Evidence and reproduction

GUIProbe creates a keyDown Option event with characters="", charactersIgnoringModifiers="e", keyCode14 and passes it to the real AKActiveCallView. Log: EMPTY_EVENT THROWS NSInvalidArgumentException: -[__NSCFConstantString characterAtIndex:]: Range or index out of bounds.

The isolated native fixture uses 191 exact production Release objects and all 42 byte-identical compiled resources, with only the app entry point replaced. It has inert synthetic call/account dependencies and an independent QA identifier. Reproduction source, log and parity manifest are retained locally under `outputs/audit-2.1.8/gui/` (`GUIProbe.m`, `verification.log`, `verification.json`).

- [NSEvent.characters](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsevent/characters): Dead keys, including Option-E, have empty characters.

issues.title: Use unique audio-device identities instead of collapsing identical device names
issues.evidence: Actual Domain mapping with synthetic unique-UID devices
issues.body:
Type: backend bug. Priority: P2. Confidence: high.

Affected: jps Telephone 2.1.8 (build 160), macOS 27.0.1 / Xcode 27. Audited main commit `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`. This is future work; source and the published build were left unchanged.

## Trigger and observed behaviour

Two audio devices expose the same customer-visible name and same input/output capability, such as two identical USB headsets with different serial/location UIDs.

SystemAudioDevices indexes each input/output by name and keeps the last duplicate. Settings saves only those names. The CoreAudio-to-PJSIP map also resolves each system device using name and direction; two distinct duplex devices therefore map to one PJSIP ID. Even choosing the first CoreAudio device as the system default cannot avoid the second mapping collapse.

Call audio or ringtone can use the wrong microphone/speaker. Backend enumeration changes after hotplug can change the selected physical device while the visible saved name stays unchanged.

## Source evidence

- [Domain/SystemAudioDevices.swift:24–45](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Domain/SystemAudioDevices.swift#L24-L45)

## Reproduction and confidence

duplicate-audio-name.swift links exact Release Domain.framework. Distinct system IDs101/102, UIDs USB:serial-one/two, identical USB Headset names and identical1-in/2-out capabilities map to backend8/8. Reversing backend enumeration gives7/7. The system name lookup similarly resolves only102.

## Future fix and regression checks

Persist CoreAudio UID per selection and distinguish duplicate labels in the UI. Carry native CoreAudio identity through the PJSIP backend mapping, rather than guessing by visible name. Migrate saved names with explicit ambiguity handling; preserve system-default behavior.

Existing coverage gap: SystemToUserAgentAudioDeviceMapTests has a same-name test, but one fixture is input-only and the other output-only; it never tests two same-direction/duplex devices. Settings persistence tests assume names are unique.

Actual model ambiguity is proven; no physical USB/Bluetooth devices or native PJSIP/CoreAudio device opens were invoked.

issues.title: Surface recording export failure and retain a durable recovery job
issues.evidence: Actual encoder/finalisation/drain; capture teardown doubled
issues.body:
Type: backend bug. Priority: P2. Confidence: high.

Affected: jps Telephone 2.1.8 (build 160), macOS 27.0.1 / Xcode 27. Audited main commit `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`. This is future work; source and the published build were left unchanged.

## Trigger and observed behaviour

A recording destination becomes unwritable or full after recording starts, or encoding otherwise fails when the call ends/quits.

CallController hides REC and uses stopRecording without its failure completion. AKSIPCall clears destination/raw-directory state before conversion. Failed conversion logs a message and leaves raw WAV files only in a private temporary directory; no UI error, persisted recovery job, automatic retry or accessible recovery path is provided. The recording drain still completes and app termination can continue.

The expected playable recording is absent or an empty reserved placeholder remains. The only captured audio can remain in temporary storage that the system is allowed to purge; the user may not know that export failed or how to recover it.

## Source evidence

- [Telephone/CallController.m:451–476](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallController.m#L451-L476)

## Reproduction and confidence

recording-finalisation-failure.m links all191 original Release production objects replacing only main. An AKSIPCall subclass stubs native recorder teardown so no SIP/audio device opens occur; production asynchronous encoder tries two valid scratch WAV tracks against an isolated read-only destination. AudioToolbox returns -54, finalisation drains, public recording/destination and recovery-directory properties clear, raw tracks remain and final placeholder is0 bytes. The harness restores scratch permissions and removes its own files.

Validation: runtime validated with actual Release AKSIPCall cleanup, AKStereoRecording encoder and drain; only native recorder teardown replaced by a safe stub.

Evidence: recording-finalisation-failure.m, build-recording-probe.py, recording-finalisation-failure.log. Scratch reproductions and logs are retained locally under `outputs/audit-2.1.8/backend/`; they contain synthetic data and do not require user credentials or real SIP calls.

## Future fix and regression checks

Propagate finalisation result to an app-level recording job/error presenter that outlives the reusable call window. Persist failed recordings and a destination/retry manifest in protected Application Support, expose retry/save-elsewhere/recover controls, and decide explicitly how quit handles a failed export.

Fail the destination after successful reservation using an isolated read-only directory or injected disk-full error. Assert visible error and durable recoverable tracks/manifest, reload the recovery job, export to a valid new destination and verify channel/data integrity and cleanup.

Existing coverage gap: Existing encoder/hardening harness detects conversion failure and checks cleanup, while the recording lifecycle model checks finalisation ownership. Neither asserts end-to-end user error propagation or recoverable-job persistence across app restart.

## Apple documentation and limits

- [Using the file system effectively](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/using-the-file-system-effectively): Temporary files are appropriate only for data that need not persist across launches; the system may purge them while the app is not running.

Conversion and cleanup failure were exercised with real local files and production encoder. Native recorder capture/teardown, real SIP audio and actual app quitting were not run.

issues.title: Drain pending call-history writes before confirming app termination
issues.evidence: Actual task/drain ordering with controlled actor delay
issues.body:
Type: source-supported shutdown persistence bug, with locally validated ordering. Priority: P2. Confidence: high on untracked-work gap; medium on natural timing frequency.

Affected: jps Telephone 2.1.8 (build 160), macOS 27.0.1 / Xcode 27. Audited main commit `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`. This is future work; source and the published build were left unchanged.

## Trigger and observed behaviour

A call disconnects shortly before Quit, or a history actor is occupied by slow file/contact/history work while SIP shutdown completes.

didDisconnect launches an unstructured Task and discards its handle. The task must hop to CallHistoryActor before adding/saving the record. finishTerminationAfterRecordings only drains the independent recording dispatch group and then replies YES to NSApplication; no history-persistence drain exists.

The app can exit while the last call-history record has not been added or durably saved, losing that call from history. Waiting for recording conversions does not establish a barrier for unrelated Swift tasks.

## Source evidence

- [UseCases/CallHistoryCallEventTarget.swift:31–40](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/UseCases/CallHistoryCallEventTarget.swift#L31-L40)
- [Telephone/AppController.m:715–742](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AppController.m#L715-L742)
- [Telephone/AKStereoRecording.m:62–70](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKStereoRecording.m#L62-L70)

## Reproduction and confidence

history-drain-order.swift uses actual Release CallHistoryCallEventTarget and AKWaitForPendingRecordingFinalizations. A semaphore holds only the disposable CallHistoryActor to model slow work; didDisconnect is invoked with a fake no-SIP call. The actual recording drain returns while the record-add factory count remains0. Releasing the actor allows the same task to run and count becomes1.

Validation: actual production task/drain ordering validated with a deliberately delayed isolated history actor; production process exit is source-supported inference.

Evidence: history-drain-order.swift, history-recording-bridge.h, history-drain-order.log. Scratch reproductions and logs are retained locally under `outputs/audit-2.1.8/backend/`; they contain synthetic data and do not require user credentials or real SIP calls.

## Future fix and regression checks

Track pending call-history persistence work in an actor/job coordinator, snapshot disconnect data before scheduling, stop accepting new events during shutdown and await/drain admitted writes before the final termination reply. Surface persistence errors separately.

Queue a disconnect event behind a controlled delayed history write, request termination with zero recordings, and assert the terminate-YES reply cannot occur before the final record is saved. Include simultaneous recording finalisation and repeated quit notifications.

Existing coverage gap: Call-history target tests await eventual record processing; recording shutdown tests/model only wait the recording group. There is no termination barrier test with a queued/slow history write.

## Apple documentation and limits

- [Task](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swift/task): Discarding the Task handle gives up the ability to await its result; launching unstructured work does not wait for completion.
- [NSApplication.reply(toApplicationShouldTerminate:)](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsapplication/reply(toapplicationshouldterminate:)): The application should send its final reply once it knows termination may proceed.

This proves independence and unsafe completion ordering under a valid delayed-actor schedule. It does not claim a real app exit or live SIP call was reproduced; SIP callback-delivery teardown issues are separately owned by the SIP audit.

issues.title: Handle failed Keychain credential saves before reporting account changes as saved
issues.evidence: Source-only ignored credential-save failure
issues.body:
Type: source-supported credential-persistence bug. Priority: P2. Confidence: high static confidence.

Affected: jps Telephone 2.1.8 (build 160), macOS 27.0.1 / Xcode 27. Audited main commit `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`. This is future work; source and the published build were left unchanged.

## Trigger and observed behaviour

The person adds an account or changes a saved password, but the login Keychain write is denied/cancelled, read-only, unavailable, full or otherwise fails.

AKKeychain.addItem returns NO on failed SecItemAdd/Update. Every current caller ignores that result. Setup persists enabled account settings before trying the credential write, closes the sheet and posts account-added. The authentication-change path uses the typed password in memory, ignores save failure and posts changed; Settings likewise proceeds after failure.

The UI reports/behaves as though an account or credential was saved, while the new secret is absent or the old password remains in Keychain. The account can fail immediately or revert to an outdated credential on restart; the person has no actionable save error.

## Source evidence

- [Telephone/AKKeychain.m:63–89](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKKeychain.m#L63-L89)

## Reproduction and confidence

Source-supported: cause SecItemAdd/Update to return a non-success code such as errSecUserCanceled or errSecReadOnly; addItem returns NO but all three callers unconditionally continue. No real Keychain fault injection was performed.

Validation: source-only by explicit audit boundary; no Security/Keychain APIs or real credentials accessed.

Evidence: AKKeychain and caller source at immutable links. Scratch reproductions and logs are retained locally under `outputs/audit-2.1.8/backend/`; they contain synthetic data and do not require user credentials or real SIP calls.

## Future fix and regression checks

Expose a typed result/error and make account setup/settings/auth-save transactions check it. Retain editable fields and report retry/cancel; do not announce durable save until credential persistence succeeds. Keep an explicit temporary-use option if intended.

Inject a credential-store double returning user-cancel/read-only/auth-failed/update-failure; assert no successful-save event or durable account change is reported and password fields remain available for retry. Test duplicate-item update and success separately.

Existing coverage gap: No current AKKeychain/caller save-error regression was found. Account/settings tests use successful/no-op credential paths rather than a throwing/failing credential store.

## Apple documentation and limits

- [Security Framework Result Codes](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/security-framework-result-codes): Apple defines distinct success, cancellation, read-only and other failure results.
- [errSecUserCanceled](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/errsecusercanceled): Cancellation means the operation was cancelled, rather than a successful credential save.

No credential values, actual Keychain state, permission prompts or real account settings were read/changed. User-visible live dialog behavior remains untested.

issues.body:
Type: known responsiveness limitation. Priority: P2. Confidence: high on synchronous UI path; medium on hardware hang occurrence.

Affected: jps Telephone 2.1.8 (build 160), macOS 27.0.1 / Xcode 27. Audited main commit `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`. This is future work; source and the published build were left unchanged.

## Trigger and observed behaviour

During an active call the person changes Sound input/output or chooses Retry Audio while a driver/backend open/stop is slow; other UI-side PJSIP operations may also wait for a global SDK lock held by the existing background outgoing-call preflight.

AppKit retry action invokes retrySoundAfterFailure synchronously. Sound preference action synchronously selects I/O while calls are active. Native selection invokes pjsua_set_snd_dev; the failure gate only reacts after that call returns. Current docs explicitly retain first-operation and shared-PJSIP-lock latency.

Telephone can become unresponsive while the native operation is blocked, before an error can be latched or Retry UI updated. Existing retry containment prevents repeated attempts but does not bound the first wait.

- [Telephone/AppController.m:238–245](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AppController.m#L238-L245)

Source-supported and previously acknowledged in AUDIO_RECOVERY.md. The synchronous call path remains in 9a32. No live microphone/SIP/driver operation or process sample was performed during this audit.

issues.title: Keep first-launch setup unchanged after rejecting whitespace-only account fields
issues.evidence: Actual first-launch wrapper/validation; startup bypassed
issues.body:
Read-only audit of **jps Telephone 2.1.8 (build 160)** on macOS 27.0.1, using the local macOS 27 SDK build. No production code or user data was changed.

# Whitespace-only first account input prematurely exits the initial setup action state

- Audit commit: `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`
- Severity: P2 / medium
- Confidence: High: actual production wrapper and Setup validation reproduced
- Classification: validated GUI state/validation bug

## Trigger

On first launch with no accounts, enter spaces only for Full Name, Domain or Username while the other required fields have nonempty text, then choose Add.

## Observed behaviour

AccountSetup correctly trims/rejects the whitespace-only value and creates no account. AppController.addAccountOnFirstLaunch then tests raw string lengths, treating that rejected submission as successful: it enables Settings and rewires Add and Cancel to the post-setup targets.

## Impact

The welcome flow changes while still displaying an invalid field and with no account created. Cancel now invokes closeSheet, which orders out the standalone welcome window; initially it performs a real window close, whose AppController notification terminates first-launch setup. The invalid submission therefore changes navigation/cancellation behaviour prematurely. No account or Keychain mutation occurs.

## Evidence

Exact production AccountSetup nib plus production AppController wrapper: savedAccounts=0, fullNameInvalid=1, Settings action becomes showPreferencePanel:, Add action becomes addAccount:, Cancel action becomes closeSheet: with AccountSetupController target. The wrapper object was intentionally allocated without init, so CompositionRoot/useragent/observers/startup never ran. This reproduces only the real wrapper transition after its real validation call.

## Suggested future fix

Advance the first-launch action state only after AccountSetup reports successful account creation, using a shared validated result or the existing account-added notification. Do not independently revalidate untrimmed field lengths.

## Limits

The exact target/action changes were reproduced without running normal AppController startup or a visible first-launch app. Termination/window-order impact is traced through the unchanged production close handlers, not executed.

## Immutable source

- [Telephone/AppController.m:305–320](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AppController.m#L305-L320)

- [Telephone/AccountSetupController.m:36–41](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AccountSetupController.m#L36-L41)
- [Telephone/AppController.m:595–605](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AppController.m#L595-L605)

## Apple guidance

- [Apple Feedback HIG](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/feedback): An invalid entry should give people a clear opportunity to correct the problem rather than silently proceed as though the task succeeded.

## Regression checks

- Use the real Setup nib and test spaces/newlines in each trimmed field with nonempty other fields. Confirm no account is added and Settings/Add/Cancel targets stay in first-launch state.
- Confirm a valid submission performs the transition once after account creation.

issues.body:
Read-only audit of **jps Telephone 2.1.8 (build 160)** on macOS 27.0.1, using the local Xcode 27 / macOS 27 SDK build. No production code or user data was changed.

- Audit commit: `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`
- Severity: P3 / layout bug; practical Dock occlusion and enabled-control reachability still need confirmation
- Confidence: High for live shown-window geometry; medium for user-visible impact
- Classification: production geometry now reproduced in an isolated **shown native window**, in both Light and Dark appearances

## Trigger and observed behaviour

Place an ordinary compact call window at the bottom of its screen’s visible work area. Increase the status text to three lines, as can occur with a longer provider diagnostic.

The body grows from 112 to 140 points. The production resize path preserves the top edge by moving the window origin down by 28 points, without keeping its bottom inside the current visible work area.

The earlier offscreen investigation has now been followed by a live WindowServer check. The Mac was available for this follow-up. **AppKit did not automatically move the shown window back into the visible work area**, including after the layout settled.

## Live evidence — Dark and Light

On this Mac, the settled visible screen area was `{{0,72},{1280,618}}`, with the whole screen `{{0,0},{1280,720}}`.

issues.title: Preserve successful transfer results after the source call is removed
issues.type: runtime callback behaviour; UI consequence source-traced
issues.evidence: Exact callback ordering with native doubles; UI inferred
issues.body:
Read-only audit of **jps Telephone 2.1.8 (build 160)** at `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`, using exact local Release callbacks on macOS 27.0.1. All tests used synthetic, isolated models; no real SIP traffic, accounts, audio, profile or Keychain access.

**Priority:** P2. **Confidence:** high; notification ordering/object loss is runtime validated against exact callbacks. Transfer-sheet presentation impact is source-traced.

**Immutable source:** [PJSUAOnCallTransferStatus.m:38–54](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/PJSUAOnCallTransferStatus.m#L38-L54), [PJSUAOnCallState.m:115–118](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/PJSUAOnCallState.m#L115-L118), [CallTransferController.m:59–63](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallTransferController.m#L59-L63), [CallTransferController.m:206–215](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallTransferController.m#L206-L215).

**Trigger and trace:** A source call receives a final 200 transfer result. The native callback first invokes `pjsua_call_hangup`, then queues its main-thread transfer notification. In bundled 2.17, hangup marks the call as hanging up and synchronously invokes the state callback; native get_info reports DISCONNECTED for that call. The state callback therefore queues its main-thread disconnect work first. That block removes the model from its account. The later transfer block looks the model up again by numeric ID, finds nothing and posts an `AKSIPCallTransferStatusDidChange` notification with nil object.

**Safe local reproduction:** Create one inert account/call model, invoke the exact compiled transfer callback with final status 200, and let its hangup double synchronously invoke the exact state callback. Drain the main queue. Observed events are first DidDisconnect with call 3, then TransferStatusDidChange with nil. The retained source object's transferStatus stays 0; an observer filtered to that source object receives 0 transfer notifications. A real SIP transfer was not attempted.

**Impact:** The protocol may complete successfully, but the source/transfer controllers never receive their source-specific success event. `CallTransferController` does not set `sourceCallTransferred`, so its successful-transfer close path is not reached; `CallController` cannot present the expected transferred status. This report does not claim that remote transfer itself fails.

**Reference:** A final REFER result is application status, not merely a request acceptance: [RFC 3515 §2.4.5](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3515.html#section-2.4.5). Callback ordering is verified in the local bundled `pjsua_call.c` at get_info lines 2559–2563 and hangup lines 3304–3313, and the corresponding [PJSIP 2.17 call implementation](https://github.com/pjsip/pjproject/blob/2.17/pjsip/src/pjsua-lib/pjsua_call.c).

**Future fix and regressions:** Preserve the source model/dialog identity before requesting hangup, or deliver final transfer state through a main-thread sequence that cannot lose the source. Publish the final result to the same source object even when it has left the agent's active-call collection; avoid matching a later reused numeric ID. Test synchronous hangup→disconnect→transfer completion, a pending transfer sheet, failure/provisional results and late notifications. Ensure the success event is delivered once.

issues.title: Attach replacement calls to a call controller
issues.type: runtime callback behaviour; UI consequence source-traced
issues.evidence: Exact callback handoff omission; live UI/provider untested
issues.body:
Read-only audit of **jps Telephone 2.1.8 (build 160)** at `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`, using exact local Release callbacks on macOS 27.0.1. All tests used synthetic, isolated models; no real SIP traffic, accounts, audio, profile or Keychain access.

**Priority:** P2. **Confidence:** high callback/UI-handoff omission; no live attended-transfer/UI scenario was run.

**Immutable source:** [PJSUAOnCallReplaced.m:37–44](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/PJSUAOnCallReplaced.m#L37-L44), [PJSUAOnIncomingCall.m:35–39](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/PJSUAOnIncomingCall.m#L35-L39), [AccountController.m:591–616](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AccountController.m#L591-L616).

**Trigger and trace:** The app is the recipient of an INVITE with Replaces for an existing call, such as the destination side of an attended transfer. The bundled library calls `on_call_replaced`, establishes/answers the new call and disconnects the old one. It takes the replacement branch instead of calling `on_incoming_call` (local bundled `pjsua_call.c`:1157–1207 and 2317–2337). The app replacement callback adds a new model but never calls the account delegate or transfers/rebinds the old call controller to it. Normal incoming callback delegation is the path that constructs a call controller, sets its call active and inserts it into `callControllers`.

**Safe local reproduction:** With exact compiled callbacks, the ordinary incoming control delivers one account delegate call and Incoming notification. A synthetic replacement 1→2 creates the new model, but delegate count remains 0. A subsequent confirmed-state callback delivers only DidConfirm for call 2; it never supplies the missing incoming/controller handoff. The model exists, so this is not a native URI parsing or native registration failure.

**Impact:** The old controller finishes with the old call while the replacement continues without a controller attached to the new call. The app cannot expose its normal hangup/mute/hold/transfer controls for that replacement and its controller-derived active-call tracking is incomplete. History incoming-event classification may also be missing, but that is not independently claimed here.

**Reference:** Replaces intentionally swaps an existing dialog for a new one; accepting it requires updating the application representation too. [RFC 3891](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc3891.html), [PJSIP 2.17 callback documentation](https://docs.pjsip.org/en/2.17/api/generated/pjsip/group/group__PJSUA__LIB__BASE.html), [bundled-equivalent replacement processing](https://github.com/pjsip/pjproject/blob/2.17/pjsip/src/pjsua-lib/pjsua_call.c).

**Future fix and regressions:** Explicitly hand the replacement to AccountController, preferably rebind the existing window/controller with a clear old/new identity transition. Do not treat the library's already-accepted replacement as an unanswered ordinary call. Verify replacement while confirmed/early, then new-call confirm, control actions and old-call disconnect; assert one controller owns the active replacement and that its eventual disconnect tears it down normally. Check unavailable/call-waiting policy deliberately.

issues.title: Guard late incoming-call delivery after an account is removed
issues.type: runtime callback and isolated consumer failure; provider race source-traced
issues.evidence: Exact callback contract plus isolated production-consumer trap
issues.body:
Read-only audit of **jps Telephone 2.1.8 (build 160)** at `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`, using exact local Release callbacks on macOS 27.0.1. All tests used synthetic, isolated models; no real SIP traffic, accounts, audio, profile or Keychain access.

**Priority:** P2. **Confidence:** confirmed callback contract failure and isolated production-consumer termination; the concurrent account-removal path is source-traced rather than reproduced with a real provider.

**Immutable source:** [PJSUAOnIncomingCall.m:32–39](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/PJSUAOnIncomingCall.m#L32-L39), [AKSIPUserAgent.m:750–758](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L750-L758), [AKSIPCallEventSource.swift:43–44](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPCallEventSource.swift#L43-L44).

**Trigger and trace:** The worker callback snapshots an incoming call and queues its application delivery to main. Before that block runs, a main-thread account removal occurs, for example while disabling an account, going Offline or restarting the agent. Delivery subsequently cannot find the account, so `addCallWithInfo` returns nil. The callback still posts Incoming with nil object. `AKSIPCallEventSource` observes Incoming for all objects and force-casts that nil object into UseCases.Call.

**Safe local reproduction:** The exact compiled incoming callback with inert models is queued; remove its fake account before draining main. Its notification object is nil, with no model or delegate delivery. Replay exactly that observed application notification into unchanged production `AKSIPCallEventSource.swift`, compiled as a standalone process with a private NotificationCenter and inert event target. It terminates with SIGTRAP (-5) at line 44: nil Optional unwrapping. See `incoming-consumer-result.json`; no SIP, real account or GUI is involved.

**Impact:** An incoming-call delivery overlapping account removal can terminate the app. This is a normal asynchronous lifecycle race, not a malformed-network-input or exploit claim. The isolated consumer proves the failing notification contract, not an end-to-end provider scenario.

**Reference:** The application explicitly dispatches the callback to main and later resolves account identity. Apple notification delivery passes the posted object to every matching unfiltered observer; GCD main-queue ordering does not make a removed account reappear. [Apple NotificationCenter.post](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/notificationcenter/post(name:object:userinfo:)), [PJSIP 2.17 application callbacks](https://docs.pjsip.org/en/2.17/api/generated/pjsip/group/group__PJSUA__LIB__BASE.html). The registration callback's controller already recognises late removal as a condition requiring an early return ([AccountController.m:497–500](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AccountController.m#L497-L500)).

**Future fix and regressions:** Validate that the account and dialog still belong to the same runtime before creating/delegating/posting; never post an incoming Call notification with nil. Coordinate rejection/cleanup of a native call only while its runtime/dialog is still current. Handle `get_info` failure instead of constructing an unchecked snapshot. Exercise removal between snapshot and main delivery, stop/restart/account-ID reuse and the normal incoming control. The consumer may additionally defend its contract, but masking producer errors alone will not make the lifecycle correct.

issues.title: Reject stale history reloads after Clear History or newer updates
issues.type: runtime validated against exact Release get-all and Contacts pipeline; visible row reappearance is source-supported inference, not a UI launch
issues.evidence: Actual async pipeline ordering with delayed matcher double
issues.body:
Read-only audit of **jps Telephone 2.1.8 (build 160)** on macOS 27.0.1. Source and user data were not changed.

**Priority:** P3. **Confidence:** high on actual pipeline result ordering; medium on natural latency frequency.
**Validation:** runtime validated against exact Release get-all and Contacts pipeline; visible row reappearance is source-supported inference, not a UI launch.

**Immutable source:** [UseCases/CallHistoryRecordGetAllUseCase.swift:33–38](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/UseCases/CallHistoryRecordGetAllUseCase.swift#L33-L38), [UseCases/ContactCallHistoryRecordGetAllUseCase.swift:31–40](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/UseCases/ContactCallHistoryRecordGetAllUseCase.swift#L31-L40), [UseCases/SimpleContactMatchingIndexFactory.swift:31–34](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/UseCases/SimpleContactMatchingIndexFactory.swift#L31-L34), [Telephone/CallHistoryViewPresenter.swift:35–40](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallHistoryViewPresenter.swift#L35-L40), [Telephone/CallHistoryViewController.swift:207–214](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallHistoryViewController.swift#L207-L214)

### Trigger
An earlier history refresh has captured records and is awaiting contact matching/another actor when Clear History succeeds and triggers a newer empty refresh. The earlier refresh completes last. Similar interleaving can follow individual deletion or rapid new-call reloads.

### Behaviour and impact
Each get-all execution starts independent untracked work and snapshots history before awaited contact enrichment. ContactsActor is reentrant across awaits. The empty refresh can reach output first while an older nonempty refresh is suspended. Neither the presenter nor view checks a request/history generation: every late result replaces the displayed records.

Deleted records can reappear in the visible history even after a successful durable deletion, until another reload. Other rapid refreshes can show stale ordering/content. This is separate from BACKEND-02: its storage deletion succeeds and underlying history stays empty.

### Safe local reproduction
history-snapshot-order.swift links the exact 9a32 Release UseCases/Domain frameworks. The real CallHistoryRecordGetAllUseCase and ContactCallHistoryRecordGetAllUseCase process an earlier one-record snapshot through a delayed isolated ContactMatching implementation. After removeAll, a second execution emits 0 rows; releasing the earlier matcher then emits 1. Output counts are exactly [0, 1] while the production history remains empty. No real Contacts database or UI was used.

**Limits:** Actual get-all/contact framework result ordering is exercised using a deliberately delayed test-double matcher. Production ContactsActor matching/index awaits and the receipt/output hop permit suspension, but the complete real Contacts/receipt/UI path was not executed. Successful on-disk deletion and visible stale rows are source-supported conditional effects, not fixture observations. No persistent records are restored by this path.

### Future fix
Carry request/history generation through snapshot, contact enrichment and presentation, accepting only the latest result. Alternatively cancel and cooperatively check previous tasks while preserving a generation guard for callbacks already queued to MainActor. Define invalidation on deletion, new records and Contacts changes.

### Regression checks
Hold the first contact match at an explicit continuation, successfully delete/clear history and complete a second refresh, then release the first. Assert the final presented records stay empty and the old result is discarded. Also interleave two nonempty snapshots and a Contacts invalidation.

### Current test gap
Get-all/contact/presenter tests validate a single refresh and eventual conversion. They do not interleave an old delayed refresh with a newer deletion/empty output or check that the final UI reflects the latest generation.

### Apple documentation
- [Protect mutable state with Swift actors](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2021/10133/) — An await allows other work/state changes before resumption; actor isolation does not preserve assumptions across suspension points.
- [Task](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swift/task) — Unstructured tasks return immediately; discarded handles cannot be awaited or cancelled by the caller.

Evidence retained outside the checkout: `history-snapshot-order.swift`, `history-snapshot-order.log`.

issues.title: End background activity when SIP startup fails
issues.type: runtime production notification adapter/target with activity doubles; native startup and energy impact source-traced
issues.evidence: Unchanged adapter/target with fake activity APIs
issues.body:
Read-only audit of **jps Telephone 2.1.8 (build 160)** on macOS 27.0.1. Production code and user data were not changed.

**Priority:** P3. **Confidence:** high for the retained token and event routing; actual energy impact was not measured.

### Source
- [Startup completion posts the event even after failure](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L323-L329).
- [The background target starts an activity unconditionally](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/BackgroundActivityUserAgentEventTarget.swift#L32-L42).
- [Stop returns immediately while the agent is stopped](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L586-L594).

### Trigger and behaviour
A native startup attempt reaches its completion with `didStart == NO`. The agent sets its state to Stopped but still posts DidFinishStarting. The production notification adapter forwards that event to BackgroundActivityUserAgentEventTarget, which retains a new `.userInitiatedAllowingIdleSystemSleep` activity token without checking `agent.isStarted`.

Calling stop while already Stopped does not emit DidFinishStopping. The latest activity therefore remains retained even though no SIP agent is running, until another start replaces it, a later successful stop clears it, or its owner is destroyed.

### Safe local reproduction
Compile the unchanged production Swift notification adapter and activity target with an inert UserAgent and a ProcessInfo subclass overriding only beginActivity/endActivity to return synthetic tokens. No real process activity or native SIP startup is invoked.

Post the normal completion event with `isStarted == false`: one token is begun and stays alive, with no end call. Repeated failed completions release the previous fake tokens but retain the newest. A later successful start/stop ends and releases its token; an ordinary success/stop control also balances correctly. The output is retained in `gui/backend-activity/verification.log` and the fixture in `main.swift`.

### Impact and limits
The app retains activity hints intended for running SIP work after failed startup. This is a lifecycle/efficiency defect; no battery-use increase or scheduler effect was measured. Idle system sleep remains allowed. There is no claim that failed retries accumulate permanently leaked activities: Apple documents that token deallocation ends an activity automatically, and the probe confirms earlier fake tokens are released when overwritten.

The real native failure and stopped-stop branch are source-traced. The probe tests their observed event/state contract through actual production Swift code without app startup, networking, accounts, audio, user settings or real begin/end APIs.

### Future fix and regression checks
Start the activity only while `agent.isStarted` is true, clear any existing token when a failed completion leaves the agent stopped, and make repeated lifecycle delivery idempotent. Keep the normal matched success/stop behaviour.

Test failed completion, repeated failures, success after failure, repeated success notification, successful stop and repeated stop. A failed/stopped agent must retain no activity token; one successful active agent must own at most one, ended once.

### Apple documentation
[ProcessInfo — Manage Activities](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/processinfo) explains matching begin/end and automatic completion when a token is deallocated. [beginActivity(options:reason:)](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/processinfo/beginactivity(options:reason:)) describes the returned activity token.

issues.evidence: Production hotplug event pipeline with inert refresh APIs, actual failure gate and Retry menu predicates
issues.title: Enable explicit audio recovery when hotplug remapping fails after null sound
issues.body:
Type: validated audio recovery bug. Priority: P2. Confidence: high on actual state/menu/event-pipeline behavior; medium on natural hardware error frequency.

Affected: jps Telephone 2.1.8 (build 160), locally audited on macOS 27.0.1 / Xcode 27 / SDK 27. Commit `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`. Production source and published build remain unchanged.

## Trigger and consequence

While a call is active, a system device-list notification refreshes the backend successfully but the following CoreAudio device/default query or PJSIP device-list query throws before native device selection. A device disappearing during its property read is one supported trigger, whose real-world frequency was not measured.

The production event fan-out first executes updateAudioDevices, which switches to null sound and reinitializes the backend, then executes sound selection. The selection use case can throw in devicesFactory.make, agent.audioDevices or soundIOFactory.make before reaching the native selection/failure gate. UserAgentEvents catches only to print; it retains pending selection but reports no audio recovery failure. Actual hasAudioFailure therefore remains false. AppController disables both the Retry menu item and its action guard, leaving no explicit recovery route through that command.

The existing active call can remain silent after the hotplug notification despite the backend refresh returning promptly and no native selection failure. The app neither announces audio-unavailable state nor permits Retry Audio. A later device/default/call event may retry the retained selection, but without that event the person has no intended explicit recovery action. No permanent loss or irrecoverable silence is claimed.

## Local evidence

Run build-hotplug-probe.py in this folder. It checks canonical source bytes, compiles the unchanged AKSIPUserAgent.m with only pjmedia_aud_subsys_init/shutdown and pjsua_get_pool_factory redirected to inert counter stubs, and links190 original Release objects plus the scratch entry/bridge objects. AppController and AKSIPUserAgent initializers are bypassed to avoid profile/SIP startup. A fake audio backend is injected into the actual AKAudioDeviceController. Actual production fan-out/refresh/selection use cases use one uniquely named synthetic duplex device, active-call model, synthetic device/default factories and inert preferences target. After healthy initial routing, separately fail each pre-selection stage. Actual native state is false, notification count0, actual menu title Retry Audio/disabled and actual retry action no-op, while the inert backend records null sound.

- **healthy-control:** refresh/null then selection(7,7) succeeds; route restored; no failure state
- **system-device-factory:** nullCount1, nativeSelectCount remains1 initial selection, actual hasAudioFailure=false, notifications0, Retry disabled and action no-op
- **default-mapping:** same missing failure/retry outcome after system/backend lists succeed
- **backend-list:** same missing failure/retry outcome after system list succeeds
- **native-selection-control:** native selection status420003 correctly latches actual failure, posts1 notification and enables Audio unavailable: Retry Audio

All failing cases recover when factories become healthy and a later didMakeCall event is delivered. Unique device names/UIDs exclude ambiguity. Every native stub returns promptly; no UI thread hang or real driver failure is needed. The preferences fan-out target still runs after the caught error.

## Immutable source

- [Telephone/CompositionRoot.swift:186–194](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CompositionRoot.swift#L186-L194)
- [Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m:934–960](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L934-L960)
- [UseCases/UserAgentSoundIOSelectionUseCase.swift:33–43](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/UseCases/UserAgentSoundIOSelectionUseCase.swift#L33-L43)
- [UseCases/UserAgentEventsUserAgentSoundIOSelectionUseCase.swift:43–53](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/UseCases/UserAgentEventsUserAgentSoundIOSelectionUseCase.swift#L43-L53)
- [Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m:846–853](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L846-L853)
- [Telephone/AppController.m:231–250](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AppController.m#L231-L250)
- [Telephone/CoreAudioSystemAudioDevicesFactory.swift:30–33](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CoreAudioSystemAudioDevicesFactory.swift#L30-L33)
- [Telephone/CoreAudioObject.swift:30–43](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CoreAudioObject.swift#L30-L43)
- [Telephone/CoreAudioDefaultSystemSoundIOFactory.swift:31–37](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CoreAudioDefaultSystemSoundIOFactory.swift#L31-L37)

## Future fix and regression checks

Represent refresh plus remapping as one audio recovery transaction. If remapping fails after switching to null sound, report a typed unavailable/recovery state through the user-agent/application boundary, notify once and make explicit Retry Audio available. Preserve the pending selection and the rule against uncontrolled automatic device reopen. Avoid inventing a success status when the route has not been restored; classify mapping errors separately from native driver errors.

Run the full ordered change-event pipeline with actual gate/menu predicates and inert backend; inject device/default/backend-list failure after successful null refresh. Assert failure UI state/notification and explicit retry availability, no implicit open loop, and successful explicit retry after the query succeeds. Include healthy remapping, a native selection failure, no-active-call behavior and stale lifecycle generation. An approved physical hotplug test should later verify audible continuity/recovery and UI notice.

Existing coverage gap: testRetriesSelectionOnNextCallWhenImmediateSelectionFails asserts retry on a later call with a throwing use-case double. It never includes the preceding destructive backend refresh or checks audio-unavailable notification and actual Retry-menu state. Individual selection/failure-gate tests cannot establish end-to-end error propagation before reaching the gate.

## Distinction from existing findings

- [#13](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/issues/13): Duplicate-name identity collapse requires two ambiguous devices and can select the wrong physical endpoint. This reproduction has one unique device and demonstrates missing recovery state after a thrown query.
- [#17](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/issues/17): Blocking native opens/SDK locks freeze the main thread. Every native stub here returns immediately; the failure is a caught Swift query error after successful refresh and disabled explicit recovery.
- [#25](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/issues/25): Background activity lifetime on startup failure is unrelated; BACKEND-09 is reserved for that already-posted finding.

## Apple contract and evidence limits

[AudioObjectGetPropertyData](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coreaudio/audioobjectgetpropertydata(_:_:_:_:_:_:)): The native property query returns an OSStatus for success or failure. Current CoreAudioObject converts non-success into a throwing query; callers must propagate recovery state after destructive refresh.

No CoreAudio/PJSIP discovery, subsystem initialization, real device open, capture, networking, profile/defaults, Keychain or Contacts operation occurred. The backend null-state marker and query failures are controlled doubles; actual updateAudioDevices control flow, hasAudioFailure, failure gate, state notification and Retry menu/action predicates were exercised. Real sound silence, visible alert, physical hotplug and complete normal app startup were not tested. Preferences update is an inert third target. No full app build, cloud run or tracked source change.

Reproduction, logs and byte/object provenance are retained locally in `outputs/audit-2.1.8/follow-up/backend/`: `HotplugRefreshProbe.swift`, `HotplugProbeBridge.m`, `HotplugProbeBridge.h`, `build-hotplug-probe.py`, `hotplug-refresh.log`, `commands.json`, `provenance.json`.

issues.title: Cancel pending account registration when Offline is selected during startup
issues.body:
Read-only follow-up audit of jps Telephone 2.1.8 (build 160), commit `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`, using local macOS 27.0.1 / Xcode 27 / SDK 27. No production source, published build, profile or provider was changed.

**Priority:** P2. **Confidence:** high for the measured controller intent/notification contract; actual provider behaviour is source-traced and untested.

**Immutable source:**

- [AccountController.m:235–253](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AccountController.m#L235-L253): requesting registration/unregistration stores deferred flags; removing the account does not clear them.
- [AccountController.m:418–435](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AccountController.m#L418-L435): Offline clears manual-unavailable state and requests removal, but leaves either deferred flag intact.
- [AccountController.m:879–890](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AccountController.m#L879-L890): a successful start completion retries the stale register/unregister intent.
- [AKSIPUserAgent.m:742–745](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L742-L745): removal is a no-op while the user agent is not yet Started.

**Supported user path:** In the main account window, choose Available or Unavailable while the engine is stopped, then choose Offline before its asynchronous startup completion is delivered. Startup is asynchronous in [AKSIPUserAgent.m:324–329](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L324-L329). This is a permitted UI choice: the saved Account.xib popup and all three menu items are enabled and have no enabled-state binding; [AccountWindowController.m:287–302](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AccountWindowController.m#L287-L302) updates Connecting presentation without disabling the popup and dispatches each chosen item. The popup subclass only adjusts alignment geometry. [AccountViewController.m:157–161](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AccountViewController.m#L157-L161) expressly retains Availability access while Offline. No WindowServer click was needed or claimed.

**Local reproduction:** `intent_probe.m` links existing Release objects and invokes the actual released lifecycle/UI-action method implementations on inert message-compatible NSObject recorders. The AccountController constructors, real account/agent/UI constructors, native start, native registration setter and its Keychain path are never invoked. The setter boundary records requested registration states; the agent records removal and reports only inert started/not-started status. A later successful registration callback is also an inert status choice rather than a network response.

Measured sequence:

1. Available while not Started records `attemptingToRegisterAccount=true` and a registration request, with Connecting presentation.
2. Offline requests removal and presents Offline, but `attemptingToRegisterAccount` remains true. The real removal method's not-Started guard confirms there is no native account to remove at this point.
3. An inert successful startup notification passed to the released completion method produces a second registration request and restores Connecting presentation.
4. An inert registered-status callback passed to the released registration handler presents Available and clears the pending flags. The newer Offline selection has been lost.

The initial Unavailable → Offline sequence exhibits the same missing cancellation through `attemptingToUnregisterAccount`: the completed start invokes unregister again. In production, unregister with no added account enters the account-add path before subsequently unregistering, so this also fails to maintain the user-selected Offline account lifecycle. No provider exchange was attempted, and this secondary sequence is not a separate issue.

**Impact:** The user selects Offline and sees it briefly, but a pending completion resumes account activity and can return the account to Available. Production calling the account-add/registration path is source-traced, not measured against a provider. The issue is the loss of the latest manual account-state intent, independent of any provider accepting or rejecting registration.

**Control / rejected suspicion:** Available → Unavailable leaves the manual-unavailable flag and pending-unregister intent set. Following completion, a synthetic registered-status callback requests unregister and never presents Available. That path matches the existing deferred-unregistration design; it is not reported as a second bug. Available unchanged correctly proceeds to Available in the same harness.

**Future fix:** Make Offline cancel both deferred register/unregister intents and any superseded startup completion action for this account. Consider representing the latest requested account state explicitly, rather than resolving two independent pending booleans in a fixed priority order. Preserve Unavailable's account-present/unregistered semantics and the shared agent's ability to start for other accounts. Ensure failure/retry presentation belongs to the current intent as well.

**Regressions:** While an inert start completion is held, select Available → Offline and Unavailable → Offline; assert neither completion nor later stale registration notification re-adds/reactivates the account or changes Offline presentation. Preserve Available unchanged and Available → Unavailable controls. Include repeated Offline/Available choices and a second account that still needs the shared agent. Use released methods and native API recorders; no real SIP or credentials are needed.

**Evidence:** `intent-results.json`, `intent-provenance.json`, `intent_probe.m`, `run_intent_probe.py`. **15 assertions pass**, comprising controller request/intent controls and saved-UI eligibility checks. Relevant released object hashes and all linked object hashes are recorded; linkage alone does not imply those other classes were exercised.

**Reference contracts:** The asynchronous start completion and account removal preconditions are verified from immutable released app source above. This finding concerns the app’s latest manual-state intent, rather than a SIP protocol violation or an assumption about a provider. Existing Foundation notification delivery is used only within the inert fixture; no online request was needed for this follow-up.

issues.body:
Read-only follow-up audit of jps Telephone 2.1.8 (build 160), locally on macOS 27.0.1 / Xcode 27 / SDK 27. Production source and published build are unchanged.

# Preserve the selected call when a full history shifts to include a new record

- Audit commit: `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`
- Severity: P2 / medium
- Confidence: High: unchanged production history sources, native table/nib and inert real event target reproduce changed identity

## Trigger

Expand history when the local Pro build has 1000 records. Select a retained record below the newest row, then let a new completed call prepend a record while the oldest is discarded.

## Observed behaviour

The shiftedByOne branch inserts row0 and removes the last row, but restoreSelection reapplies the old numeric index. The selected identity moves to its previous neighbour, despite the original record still being present. Return invokes the newly selected identity.

## Impact

An asynchronous valid history refresh can change the record a keyboard user is about to redial or delete. The native probe records a different call identifier on Return. No live call, actual deletion, data corruption or privacy incident is asserted.

## Native evidence

Native exact-nib probe: LIMIT_BEFORE rows=1000 selected=1 chosen=R1; LIMIT_AFTER rows=1000 selected=1 expectedRetainedRow=2; LIMIT_RETURN chosen=R0 expectedRetainedIdentity=R1. The conditional non-Pro three-record preview also reproduces B→A after [A,B,C]→[X,A,B], but that receipt-limited branch is not active in this LocalPro build.

Reproduction source: `FollowupProbe.swift`; observed output: `verification.log`; component/resource parity: `verification.json`. All live outside the repository.

## Suggested future fix

Capture the selected record identifier before updating the array and resolve it in the updated records after the table change. Use an explicit nearby-row fallback when the selected record was actually removed. Preserve compact mode’s intentional newest-record behaviour.

## Regression checks

- Expanded 1000-record history: selecting R1, then prepending NEW and dropping R999 keeps R1 selected at row2; Return uses R1.
- Retained selected first/middle/penultimate records remain selected through capped shifts; an evicted selected oldest record chooses a documented fallback.
- Ordinary uncapped prepend, identity-preserving metadata refresh, explicit deletion and collapsed one-recent behaviour retain their existing contracts.

## Limits and duplicate review

History constructors are optimised out of the Release object symbols, so seven byte-unchanged history sources were recompiled locally alongside two original Release row/date objects and all 42 byte-identical Release Resources. The probe invokes the actual source action/event-target methods with inert factories. It does not start normal AppController, accounts, Contacts, receipt validation, SIP/audio or persistence. This finding is independent of the clickedRow suspicion, which root’s visible native menu-dismiss checks disproved.

Distinct from published #24: no stale or out-of-order reload is required. A correct newest capped snapshot is applied, but the selected identity is restored incorrectly.

## Immutable source

- [Telephone/RestoredSelectionIndex.swift:22–30](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/RestoredSelectionIndex.swift#L22-L30)
- [Telephone/CallHistoryViewController.swift:208–237](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallHistoryViewController.swift#L208-L237)
- [Telephone/CallHistoryViewController.swift:117–121](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallHistoryViewController.swift#L117-L121)
- [Telephone/CompositionRoot.swift:201–209](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CompositionRoot.swift#L201-L209)
- [UseCases/TruncatingCallHistory.swift:35–39](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/UseCases/TruncatingCallHistory.swift#L35-L39)

## Current primary Apple sources

- [Focus and selection HIG](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/focus-and-selection/): Focus and selection communicate the object targeted by interaction. Keeping stable identity during an unrelated update is the audit’s application of that guidance, not a quoted Apple API requirement.
- [NSTableView.selectedRow](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nstableview/selectedrow): The native selectedRow is an index; the application must correctly map it to the intended item after changing data.
