# Apply a changed ringtone output while an incoming call is ringing

Type: backend/settings correctness. Priority: P3. Confidence: high for actual released use-case composition; physical playback untested.

Audited jps Telephone 2.1.8 (build 160), main commit `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`, locally on macOS 27.0.1 / Xcode 27 / SDK 27. Production source and build remain unchanged.

## Trigger and consequence

While at least one incoming call is unanswered and the ringtone is playing, select a different ringtone output in Settings → Sound.

The Sound preference handler saves the selected device and invokes RingtoneOutputUpdateUseCase. Its stop/start sequence receives the same ConditionalRingtonePlaybackUseCase used for ordinary call events. That guard suppresses stop while any incoming call remains unanswered. DefaultRingtonePlaybackUseCase then starts the existing cached ringtone rather than creating a sound from the new settings.

The current ringtone retains its old output configuration, despite the settings change. The next newly created ringtone can apply the new output after ringing ends. This does not establish permanent routing loss, actual silence or a missed call.

## Component reproduction and controls

`RingtoneReconfigurationProbe.swift` links the exact released UseCases/Domain frameworks. Only ringtone/factory/delegate models are inert. The factory records which synthetic device is used when production playback constructs a ringtone.

1. Start production guarded playback with synthetic output A and an unanswered-call guard.
2. Change the factory's desired configuration to output B.
3. Invoke the actual RingtoneOutputUpdateUseCase.
4. Observe factoryCount=1, existing tone=A, startCount=2, stopCount=0. No new configuration is loaded.

Controls pass: idle output update does not start ringing; the unguarded stop/start creates a new tone B and stops A; after the unanswered-call state ends, normal stop/start creates B. Four scenarios passed.

The synthetic desired-device setter represents the source-confirmed settings/factory boundary; actual preferences UI, NSSound and sound hardware were not invoked. Production composition and preference/factory paths below establish the normal caller of the measured use case.

## Immutable source

- [CompositionRoot.swift:67–80](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CompositionRoot.swift#L67-L80): cached playback is wrapped in the unanswered-call stop guard.
- [SoundPreferencesViewEventTarget.swift:51–55](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/SoundPreferencesViewEventTarget.swift#L51-L55): save selection, select call sound I/O, update ringtone output.
- [CompositionRoot.swift:150–158](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CompositionRoot.swift#L150-L158): output update receives the guarded playback.
- [RingtoneOutputUpdateUseCase.swift:27–33](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/UseCases/RingtoneOutputUpdateUseCase.swift#L27-L33).
- [ConditionalRingtonePlaybackUseCase.swift:33–41](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/UseCases/ConditionalRingtonePlaybackUseCase.swift#L33-L41).
- [AKSIPUserAgent+ConditionalRingtonePlaybackUseCaseDelegate.swift:19–22](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent%2BConditionalRingtonePlaybackUseCaseDelegate.swift#L19-L22).
- [DefaultRingtonePlaybackUseCase.swift:34–45](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/UseCases/DefaultRingtonePlaybackUseCase.swift#L34-L45).
- [NSSoundToSoundAdapterFactory.swift:20–33](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/NSSoundToSoundAdapterFactory.swift#L20-L33): only newly made sound configuration updates playbackDeviceIdentifier.

## Future fix and regressions

Separate reconfiguration from the conditional call-event stop. Permit an explicit ringtone-output change to recreate or update the active sound atomically while preserving ringing for every remaining unanswered call. Keep the guard that prevents ending one call from silencing another incoming call. Handle construction failure without losing a working ring.

Test the real guarded composition while an incoming call is unanswered, change output and assert the active configuration changes; repeat with multiple incoming calls. Check idle behaviour, no unnecessary rings, ordinary call-end stop suppression, later final stop, and failed reconstruction. A subsequent authorised physical playback check should verify the selected device.

Existing RingtoneOutputUpdateUseCaseTests uses a stop/start spy; it does not compose the conditional guard and cached real playback.

## Apple contract, duplicates and limits

Apple's [NSSound playbackDeviceIdentifier](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nssound/playbackdeviceidentifier-swift.property?language=objc) identifies the sound's output device. The defect is the app's update path never reaching the factory/property update; this is not a claim of an NSSound or macOS 27 regression.

Distinct from #13 device-name ambiguity, #17 native audio-open blocking and #26 call-audio remapping failure. These controls use one unique synthetic output at a time, and concern the separate ringtone playback path.

Evidence retained locally under `outputs/audit-2.1.8/repeated/root/`: `RingtoneReconfigurationProbe.swift`, `build-ringtone-probe.py`, `ringtone-reconfiguration.log`, `ringtone-provenance.json`. No normal app, NSApplication, profile/defaults, real preferences, Contacts, Keychain, device discovery/open, sound playback/capture or SIP operation occurred.

issues.title: Keep the selected contact destination attached to its own token
issues.evidence: Released native token methods/field editor with synthetic Contacts and destination recorder
issues.body:
Observed in 2.1.8 (build 160), frozen main commit 9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25, using local macOS 27.0.1 / SDK 27.

A contact token's selected phone number is stored in one controller-wide index. Converting a second input resets that index even before the input is accepted. The existing contact can therefore silently switch numbers, or a shorter token can raise an out-of-bounds exception when the later token chooses a higher index.

Safe reproduction and measured result:
1. A synthetic contact has two destinations, 100 and 200. Convert the entered number 200 with the unchanged production token delegate. It returns two destinations and chooses index 1; the actual callDestinationURI getter returns 200.
2. Convert an additional unknown destination 300. That conversion sets the same index to 0. The original first token now resolves to 100, although no menu action changed its selected number.
3. The production rounded-token rejection branch returns nil for the extra token, but the original token still resolves to 100 after the rejected conversion.
4. A native unshown NSTokenTextView field editor, using the real delegate and compiled field nib, commits the appended 300 input and leaves two tokens/index 0/first destination 100. The makeCall guard accepts the first token. No call is placed.
5. Reverse order—one-number token followed by a token selecting index 1—raises the actual NSRangeException in displayStringForRepresentedObject for the shorter token. The probe catches it; this does not claim a guaranteed whole-app crash.
6. Negative control: a single two-number contact, with no later conversion, remains 200.

Trace: representedObjectForEditingString sets callDestinationURIIndex for every conversion; display/edit/menu delegates and callDestinationURI use that global index for a supplied token or the first token. makeCall takes the first token and forwards callDestinationURI to AccountController.makeCallToURI. shouldAddObjects blocks extra rounded tokens only after conversion and returns nil rather than the documented empty-array rejection.

Immutable source:
- https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/ActiveAccountViewController.m#L82-L98
- https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/ActiveAccountViewController.m#L249-L277
- https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/ActiveAccountViewController.m#L672-L691
- https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/ActiveAccountViewController.m#L835-L983
- https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/ActiveAccountViewController.m#L1023-L1029
- https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/Base.lproj/ActiveAccountView.xib#L20-L34

Apple contracts: [represented-object conversion](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nstokenfielddelegate/tokenfield(_:representedobjectforediting:)) maps an individual editing string to its represented object; [token validation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nstokenfielddelegate/tokenfield(_:shouldadd:at:)) documents empty-array rejection and says nil causes an error. These are current AppKit contracts, not a new macOS 27-only HIG mandate.

Future fix: store the chosen destination with its represented token or enforce a single token before mutating existing selection. Reject extra inputs with an empty array, and guard every supplied token's type/index before subscripting. Preserve the selected number until an explicit change of that token.

Regression checks: two-number contact selecting its second number then append/reject plain input; a short token followed by a later multi-number contact; paste/commit multiple inputs; changing a contact's menu choice; one-token normal control; ensure the call destination and displayed/editable representation agree.

Evidence boundary: the local probe links 191 byte-identical released application objects, replacing only main.o, and 42 exact released resources. The real conversion/getter/delegate paths run with inert synthetic AddressBook records and fake search constructors; shared defaults are redirected to a unique scratch suite with volatile registration. No real Contacts lookup, account/controller startup, credential access, SIP/media/audio or user settings write occurs. Native field editing is unshown; visible user interaction and provider calls remain untested. Probe: outputs/audit-2.1.8/repeated/gui/TokenIndexProbe.m; observations token-index-verification.log; hashes token-index-verification.json. Distinct from existing UTF8/port conversion and history row-identity issues.

issues.body:
Observed in 2.1.8 (build 160), frozen main commit 9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25.

Opening Transfer while a call is already manually held does not introduce a new hold. Closing the initial transfer setup then unconditionally toggles that held source call, requesting Resume even though the user did not resume it.

Measured production-method reproduction:
- Already-held active source: showCallTransferSheet performs 0 hold toggles and begins 1 sheet. closeSheet performs 1 toggle, ends 1 sheet and leaves the source unheld.
- Previously unheld active source (negative control): opening performs 1 toggle; closing performs the second toggle and restores unheld state as intended.

The actual ActiveCallViewController menu validation allows transfer on a confirmed local-held call (only remote-held calls are excluded). The initial transfer nib's Close action routes to closeSheet. Its condition checks only current active/held state, without recording whether the transfer UI caused the hold. CallController.toggleCallHold forwards the request to the source call.

- https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/ActiveCallViewController.m#L222-L230
- https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/ActiveCallViewController.m#L408-L422

Future fix: record the source's hold state when opening each transfer session, and resume on cancellation only when that session put it on hold. Reset the session ownership after dismissal, distinguish user hold changes and remote hold, and preserve existing normal transfer recovery.

Regression checks: confirmed call already locally held → open Transfer → Close stays held; confirmed unheld → open/close restores unheld; source disconnects while sheet open; failed hold; remote-hold transitions; repeated sheet sessions do not carry old hold ownership.

Evidence boundary: local probe links 191 original Release application objects and 42 exact resources. The two exact released method implementations execute on inert message-compatible source/sheet recorders, capturing hold toggles and begin/end calls. The native call implementation and audio are not run, so the established defect is an unexpected Resume request/state transition; real provider/audio effect is source-supported, not measured. No normal app/controller startup, real account, Contacts, Keychain, SIP, audio or defaults write. Probe: NativeStateProbe.m / native-state-verification.log / native-state-verification.json. issues.body:
Read-only audit of jps Telephone 2.1.8 (build 160), frozen main commit `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`, locally on macOS 27.0.1 / Xcode 27 / SDK 27. Production source and build remain unchanged.

- [Telephone/AccountControllers.m:138–149](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AccountControllers.m#L138-L149)
- [Telephone/AccountController.m:418–435](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AccountController.m#L418-L435)
- [Telephone/AccountController.m:503–516](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AccountController.m#L503-L516)
- [Telephone/AccountController.m:897–900](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AccountController.m#L897-L900)
- [Telephone/AccountController.m:591–596](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AccountController.m#L591-L596)

`AppController.workspaceSessionDidBecomeActive:` invokes `registerAllAccounts`; wake invokes `registerReachableAccounts` when the session is active. Both collection methods iterate enabled accounts without testing manual Unavailable intent. Conversely, `AccountController.networkReachabilityDidBecomeReachable:` explicitly tests `!isAccountUnavailable` before registering. The successful-registration handler then calls `setAccountUnavailable:NO` and `showAvailableState` when no deferred unregister is pending. The incoming handler's manual-unavailable branch normally answers 480, so losing this flag also removes that suppression; no incoming call was generated in the probe.

**Ordinary trigger:** Leave an enabled account in the stable Unavailable state, then switch the user session away and back, or sleep/wake while that account's registrar is reachable and the session is active. There is no pending manual registration required for this defect. Apple's [sessionDidBecomeActiveNotification](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsworkspace/sessiondidbecomeactivenotification) documents session switch-in, and [didWakeNotification](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsworkspace/didwakenotification) documents device wake. The app registers those workspace notifications at AppController:154–163. These are normal lifecycle handlers; the reproduction calls them directly with inert collaborators rather than emitting OS events.

**Local evidence:** `automatic_intent_probe.m` invokes exact existing Release method implementations on inert message-compatible NSObject recorders. It invokes the actual manual menu-selection path to establish `accountUnavailable=YES`, then seeds a stable completed-unregistration state. No native request or provider response is produced. The registration setter only records intent; startup completion and successful registered status are inert acknowledgements passed to actual released handlers.

Measured traces:

- Stable Unavailable + ordinary reachability: no registration request; manual flag remains true (negative control).
- Stable Unavailable + session activation: registration request true; inert successful-registration acknowledgement clears the manual flag and presents Available.
- Stable Unavailable + reachable wake after stopped-agent/account removal: registration request true and deferred-start registration; inert start completion repeats the request, then the registered acknowledgement clears the manual flag and presents Available.
- Unreachable wake, inactive-session wake and disabled-account wake: no registration request and manual flag retained (negative controls).
- Available intent + session activation/reachability: ordinary registration and Available presentation remain correct.

**31 assertions pass**, including native-method state/request traces and production saved-UI eligibility. Results and object hashes/link command are in `intent-results.json` and `intent-provenance.json`. No AppController/account/controller/user-agent initializer, NSApplication, window, defaults, Keychain, hardware, provider, socket, SIP endpoint, protocol input or OS session/sleep action was invoked. Full object linkage resolves symbols only; it does not exercise all linked classes.

**Impact and limits:** The bug is a demonstrated loss of persistent manual availability intent under automatic lifecycle processing. A successful real provider registration would allow the account to be presented/handled as Available, but actual provider traffic or incoming-call effects are source inferences, not runtime claims. This is distinct from issue #27/SIP-07: that issue concerns a newer **Offline** choice cancelling an already pending start request; this one begins with stable **Unavailable** and no pending intent, and is caused by unguarded automatic registration policy.

**Future fix:** Represent/preserve the latest manual availability intent through automatic registration helpers. At minimum, skip manually unavailable accounts during wake/session auto-registration, or explicitly retain their unregister/suppression intent if temporary registration is needed for another purpose. Apply the same policy consistently to all automatic registration/restart paths without preventing an explicit Available selection from registering or disturbing other enabled accounts. Do not remove Unavailable's account-present/unregistered semantics.

**Regression expectations:** Stable manual Unavailable across session-resign/active, stopped-agent reachable wake/start completion, ordinary reachability and app-controlled restart; verify no implicit Available transition and no lost incoming-suppression flag. Include available, disabled, unreachable and inactive-session controls, multiple accounts and explicit Available after Unavailable. Isolated lifecycle recorders suffice for intent tests; actual provider/OS integration should be a separate test.

**API reference:** PJSIP [2.17 account API](https://docs.pjsip.org/en/2.17/api/generated/pjsip/group/group__PJSUA__LIB__ACC.html) specifies that `pjsua_acc_set_registration(..., renew=0)` starts unregistration and that configured account add starts registration. The app's `AKSIPAccount.setRegistered:` maps true/false to those calls. No SIP protocol violation or provider-specific assumption is required for the finding.

issues.title: Invalidate pending history additions when deleting an account
issues.evidence: Actual history remove/add use cases and delayed scratch-file write with successful deletion control
issues.body:
**Priority:** P2. **Evidence:** reproduced durable ordering failure in isolated production components; ordinary app interaction timing remains source-traced.

**Version:** 2.1.8/build 160; source `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`; local macOS 27.0.1, Xcode/SDK 27. No source changes.

**Trigger and trace:** A completed call has queued its history addition, and its account is deleted before the addition finishes. [CallHistoryCallEventTarget.swift:30–38](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/UseCases/CallHistoryCallEventTarget.swift#L30-L38) first obtains the history, then its factory returns an addition use case that launches another Task ([CallHistoryRecordAddUseCase.swift:31–35](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/UseCases/CallHistoryRecordAddUseCase.swift#L31-L35)). In parallel, [account deletion](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/UseCases/CallHistoriesHistoryRemoveUseCase.swift#L24-L29) clears the history and removes it from the cache. Cache removal does not invalidate a previously held object ([DefaultCallHistories.swift:31–47](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/UseCases/DefaultCallHistories.swift#L31-L47)); a later [persistent add saves to the same file](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/UseCases/PersistentCallHistory.swift#L47-L75).

**Safe local reproduction:** `repeated/backend/history-removal-race.swift` links exact released UseCases/Domain frameworks with byte-identical SimplePropertyListStorage. A synthetic Call/Account and one factory latch hold the real disconnect task after history acquisition. The factory returns the actual production addition use case. Actual CallHistoriesHistoryRemoveUseCase successfully deletes a private scratch plist; the file is absent and no storage error occurs. Resume the addition: the file is recreated with one completed call, and a new actual history lookup reloads it. Negative control runs the same production removal use case after additions have completed: the file stays absent. Build commands, input hashes and log are retained outside the checkout.

**Impact and deduplication:** A successfully deleted account's call-history bytes can return. The removed account has no necessary visible window, so immediate visible resurrection is not claimed. This differs from #4 (failed deletion), #15 (quit before pending writes), and #24 (stale presentation while the history itself remains empty).

**Contract:** Apple documents the immediate-return lifetime of unstructured [Task](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swift/task/). An [atomic file write](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/nsdata/writingoptions/atomic) does not implement logical cancellation or an account-deletion barrier.

**Future fix:** Invalidate that UUID/history generation before deleting storage, and reject delayed work for the removed account. Alternatively drain/serialize additions and deletion in one actor-owned operation with an account tombstone. Preserve intentional new-account creation separately.

**Regression checks:** Hold an addition after history acquisition; remove the account; resume and assert no file/cache is recreated. Repeat deletion before acquisition, before the nested add and after completed additions. Verify another account and a new UUID continue to persist normally.

**Limits:** No normal app, user account/history, provider, Contacts, Keychain, audio device or OS settings were touched. The latch establishes a possible scheduler interleaving, not its frequency; Settings-to-removal notification wiring is source-traced. All fixture data is synthetic and private scratch files are removed.

issues.title: Recognise documented CoreAudio errors from implicit SDK sound opens
issues.evidence: Released error gate, SDK 27 CoreAudio constants and source-traced vendored PJSIP return path
issues.body:
**Priority:** P2. **Evidence:** exact released recovery gate plus real macOS 27 constants and vendored mapping; native hardware consequence source-traced.

**Version:** 2.1.8/build 160, source `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`; local macOS 27.0.1/SDK 27. No source changes.

**Trigger and trace:** After idle audio closes, PJSUA's make-call path may reopen sound internally. The bundled 2.17 source calls `pjsua_set_snd_dev` and returns its error before making the call (`pjsua_call.c:923–928`). The audio backend maps errors from AudioUnitInitialize/AudioOutputUnitStart using [the vendored mapping](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/ThirdParty/PJSIP/include/pjmedia-audiodev/errno.h#L95-L104): `440000 - OSStatus`. Positive hardware fourcc values therefore map negative. [AKAudioDeviceController.m:20–29](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKAudioDeviceController.m#L20-L29) recognises only `stop` among negatives. [Actual make-call completion](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPAccount.m#L336-L362) releases admission and reports the raw result, but [reportAudioFailure](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKAudioDeviceController.m#L213-L218) does not latch these documented errors.

**Safe reproduction:** `repeated/backend/audio-fourcc-gate.m` links the exact released AKAudioDeviceController object with an inert backend. Real SDK constants and the real macro yield `!dev=-559787702`, `nrdy=-1852550585`, `what=-2002889396`, `!hog=-560052391`. Reporting each as make-call failure leaves `hasFailed=false`, notification/fallback counts 0, and admits the next outgoing request. The mapped `stop` control latches, falls back once and blocks admission. Unrelated `PJ_EINVAL` and `-1` controls remain clear. No PJSUA endpoint or audio hardware is initialised. Logs, build commands and source/framework/object hashes are retained locally.

**Impact:** A failed implicit hardware open can produce Call Failed without entering the app's explicit audio recovery state. Another call remains admitted to retry the failing open. Physical driver failure frequency, actual audible state and repeated driver hangs were not measured. Explicit device-selection uses the separate any-error gate and is not this trigger.

**References:** Apple defines [bad device](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coreaudio/kaudiohardwarebaddeviceerror) and related statuses; macOS 27 AudioHardwareBase.h confirms the values. The exact bundled pjproject-2.17 archive, including coreaudio_dev.m create/start and pjsua_aud.c sound-open return paths, was inspected. [Version-specific upstream CoreAudio source](https://github.com/pjsip/pjproject/blob/2.17/pjmedia/src/pjmedia-audiodev/coreaudio_dev.m) is a reference; local vendored source is authoritative because its line numbering differs.

**Deduplication:** #26 fails in Swift remapping before the native failure gate; here a mapped native result reaches the classifier but is not recognised. #17 covers blocking/threading, which is separate from failure/admission state.

**Future fix and regressions:** Prefer typed audio provenance; otherwise audit specific SDK/vendored mapped fourcc statuses with wide arithmetic. Do not classify every negative number as audio. Cover mapped documented failures through completion/notification/admission, existing stop/positive errors, unrelated SIP/PJ_EINVAL/-1 and overflow controls, then explicit retry and healthy operation. Answer/media reports share the classifier, but propagation of all codes through every API is not asserted.

**Limits:** Actual gate/macro results are reproduced. Native implicit-open propagation, Retry Audio/UI consequence and physical errors are source-traced only. No user profile, provider, device, Contacts, Keychain or OS setting was touched.

issues.title: Release failed reachability initialisers exactly once
issues.evidence: Byte-identical reachability initializer with inert native boundary lifetime recorder
issues.body:
**Priority:** P2. **Evidence:** production ARC initialiser/deallocator with inert C boundary recorders; possible native process failure is a contract consequence.

**Version:** 2.1.8/build 160, source `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`; local macOS 27.0.1/SDK 27. Source unchanged.

**Trigger and trace:** Callback registration or run-loop scheduling fails while constructing the account's reachability object. [Both failure branches](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKNetworkReachability.m#L82-L99) release `_reachability`, then return nil without clearing the ivar. ARC destroys the partially initialised object; [dealloc](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKNetworkReachability.m#L106-L110) unconditionally unschedules that released pointer and releases it again.

**Safe local reproduction:** Byte-identical production AKNetworkReachability.m is compiled with only five C calls redirected: hostname target creation, set callback, schedule, unschedule and release. They use/count an inert marker, so no real network operation or actual double free occurs. Inject callback failure: releases 2, schedule 0, unschedule 1 after release. Inject scheduling failure: releases 2, schedule 1, unschedule 1 after release. Healthy setup: one release; unschedule happens before release. `repeated/backend/reachability-cleanup.m`, boundary header, logs, command list and input hashes are retained locally.

**Impact:** Ordinary reachability setup failure can lead to invalid native-handle use and a double release instead of a clean unavailable state. An actual crash or current frequency of these API failures was not measured. This is an ownership/error-path bug; deprecation alone is not the finding.

**Contracts:** Apple documents [scheduling failure as FALSE](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/systemconfiguration/scnetworkreachabilityschedulewithrunloop(_:_:_:)) and requires a non-null live target. [Core Foundation ownership rules](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/CoreFoundation/Conceptual/CFMemoryMgmt/Concepts/Ownership.html) require relinquishing owned references once when finished. SDK 27 headers confirm these failure contracts.

**Future fix and regressions:** Centralise handle ownership cleanup, clear any released ivar, guard null/partially configured state, and unschedule only a successfully scheduled live target. Cover creation failure, callback-set failure, scheduling failure and a healthy lifetime with exactly one release per created handle and no post-release use. A future NWPathMonitor migration should retain explicit cleanup/error ownership.

**Limits:** Production Objective-C init/dealloc ordering is measured; actual SystemConfiguration failure, native crash, network state, SIP provider and user account/profile remain untested. No repository changes or real user data were involved.

issues.title: Recover empty Sound settings after a transient device query failure
issues.evidence: Released Sound controller and unchanged loader/presenter with throwing-then-healthy provider, cached lifecycle and explicit retry controls
issues.body:
**Priority:** P2. **Evidence:** exact released Sound controller plus production loading/presentation components, with inert provider/settings/menu boundaries.

**Version:** 2.1.8/build 160, source `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`, local macOS 27.0.1/SDK 27. Source unchanged.

**Trigger and trace:** The first visit to Settings > Sound encounters a transient CoreAudio enumeration/property error. [SettingsSoundIOLoadUseCase](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/UseCases/SettingsSoundIOLoadUseCase.swift#L43-L48) throws before publishing any devices. [The event target catches this and only prints to the log](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/SoundPreferencesViewEventTarget.swift#L70-L77). The three device menus are initially empty in [the nib](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/Base.lproj/SoundPreferencesView.xib#L25-L87). [SoundPreferencesViewController](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/SoundPreferencesViewController.m#L62-L81) initiates loading in awakeFromNib and has no appearance retry or displayed failure state. [PreferencesController retains the same Sound controller](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/PreferencesController.m#L104-L110) when changing sections or reopening Settings. Once the transient query recovers, ordinary revisits still show empty device menus. Only an explicit [updateSoundIO](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/SoundPreferencesViewController.m#L114-L126), normally supplied by a later device-change notification, retries loading.

**Safe local reproduction:** `repeated/backend/sound-pane-retry.swift` links the exact released SoundPreferencesViewController object and exact UseCases/Domain frameworks. Byte-identical production Swift event target/factory/presenter code is compiled with an in-memory settings implementation and synthetic throwing-then-healthy device provider. A detached controller uses menu stand-ins which retain its real NSMenus; no nib, popup, visible window or application is started. The unrelated ringtone-library/defaults read is suppressed by the fixture subclass. Initial failure gives provider queries=1 and three empty device menus. Mark the provider healthy and call the actual controller appearance/disappearance callbacks twice on the same instance: queries remains 1 and menus remain empty. Explicit updateSoundIO then gives queries=2 and populates all menus. A healthy initial-load control also populates all three menus. Logs, exact build arguments, source/object/framework hashes are retained.

**Impact:** A temporary query problem leaves all three audio-device selectors unusable for the rest of the cached pane's lifetime unless a qualifying update arrives or the app is restarted. The user sees empty selectors without an explanation or retry. Physical driver error frequency and the full normal-app reopening flow were not exercised; cached ownership/reopen wiring and empty nib menus are source-traced. No nil-selection crash is claimed.

**Apple contract:** [awakeFromNib](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/objectivec/nsobject-swift.class/awakefromnib()) belongs to nib loading, whereas [viewWillAppear](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsviewcontroller/viewwillappear()) runs when a loaded view becomes visible. SDK 27 headers confirm this distinction. Retrying a failed load when the pane appears, or offering a clear accessible Retry action, is a future design choice; Apple does not mandate a particular retry implementation.

**Deduplication:** #26 concerns native audio recovery failing to latch during a hotplug Swift remapping error. This trigger is the first Settings data load, the persisted empty view state, and missing recovery on a normal revisit; it does not need a call, native sound-open failure or hotplug notification.

**Future fix and regressions:** Track failed loading explicitly and retry on a later appearance or user Retry. Preserve any last valid device selections during later failures and keep the failure state accessible. Cover a failed first query followed by healthy revisit, failed repeated retries, normal healthy load, a later device-update recovery, and healthy saved selections. Keep these checks synthetic; avoid automatically opening real audio devices just to render Settings.

**Limits:** Loader/menu behavior is measured in isolated production components and manually invoked native lifecycle methods. Real nib decoding, container/window-driven lifecycle, physical CoreAudio errors and user profile are source-traced or untested. No SIP, audio discovery/open/capture, real settings, Contacts, Keychain, visible UI or OS preferences were used.

issues.title: Prune expired history subscribers from shared event lists
issues.evidence: Released weak subscriber collections retain 200 obsolete wrappers after 100 lifecycle cycles; all origins released, live control delivers once
issues.body:
**Priority:** P3 maintenance. **Evidence:** exact released event collections and weak wrappers with synthetic subscribers; app lifecycle connection source-traced. No source changes.

**Version:** 2.1.8/build 160; source `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`; local macOS 27.0.1/SDK 27.

**Trigger and trace:** Repeated account disable/enable retires and replaces account controllers ([AppController.m:405–434](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AppController.m#L405-L434)). Each new history view constructs an event target ([AccountViewController.m:135–145](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AccountViewController.m#L135-L145)), whose [factory appends fresh weak wrappers](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallHistoryViewEventTargetFactory.swift#L79-L81) to app-lifetime shared lists. [StoreEventTargets](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/UseCases/StoreEventTargets.swift#L20-L65) and [DayChangeEventTargets](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/UseCases/DayChangeEventTargets.swift#L19-L34) append strongly retained entries and have no removal/pruning path. Their wrappers correctly hold weak origins ([store wrapper](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/UseCases/WeakStoreEventTarget.swift#L20-L29), [day wrapper](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/UseCases/WeakDayChangeEventTarget.swift#L19-L28)); once an origin is released the wrapper becomes a permanent empty entry.

**Local validation:** `repeated/root/SubscriberRetentionProbe.swift` links the exact released UseCases/Domain frameworks. One hundred synthetic registration/release cycles release all 200 real subscribers, confirmed through weak references, while retaining 100 store wrappers and 100 day wrappers. Read-only Mirror introspection counts the actual private arrays. Dispatching the real store/day callbacks leaves those counts unchanged. An added live subscriber receives exactly one callback in each collection. Logs, compiler arguments and released framework hashes are retained outside the checkout.

**Impact and limits:** Small obsolete wrappers and event fan-out accumulate within the process as account/history views are recreated. This is unnecessary bookkeeping and a bounded maintenance issue. The fixture does **not** show a retained history view, wrong event delivery, visible sluggishness, a measured performance regression or memory growth across launches. It does not drive actual account toggles or purchases; their connection to new registrations is source-traced.

**Future cleanup:** Introduce removable registration tokens or a weak-entry collection that prunes expired origins before adding/dispatching. Preserve live subscribers and ordering, including asynchronous store callbacks. Avoid a strong-retention fix that would retain old views.

**Regression checks:** Repeat registration/release cycles and assert obsolete entries are removed; assert live origins remain subscribed exactly once; cover pruning around asynchronous purchase/restore callbacks and normal day changes. No provider, real purchases, user profile, Contacts, Keychain, audio hardware, normal app startup or visible UI was used.

**Deduplication:** #2 concerns unused Objective-C helper categories. This is reachable, obsolete listener bookkeeping with an observed lifecycle consequence; no currently reachable history feature is proposed for removal.

issues.title: Handle nullable DNS watcher creation before using Core Foundation handles
issues.evidence: Byte-identical DNS watcher with inert CoreFoundation boundaries; creator-failure and healthy cleanup controls
issues.body:
**Priority:** P2. **Evidence:** byte-identical production initialiser/deallocator with inert C boundary counts. Native crash is a documented contract consequence, not an executed crash.

**Version:** 2.1.8/build 160, source `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`, local macOS 27.0.1/SDK 27. Source unchanged.

**Trigger and trace:** SystemConfiguration fails to create the DNS dynamic-store session or its run-loop notification source while the app initialises. [CompositionRoot creates NameServers unconditionally](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CompositionRoot.swift#L291-L294), including when Use DNS SRV is disabled. [NameServers.m:38–46](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/NameServers.m#L38-L46) checks neither nullable creator result. A NULL store is passed into notification/source setup; a NULL source is passed to CFRunLoopAddSource and CFRelease. If the store creation failed, [dealloc also releases the NULL store](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/NameServers.m#L51-L53). The initialiser has no unavailable/error state and returns an object if inert boundaries let execution continue.

**Safe local reproduction:** `repeated/backend/nameservers-init.m` compiles byte-identical NameServers.m with six C calls redirected to inert markers/counters: dynamic-store creation, notification-key registration, run-loop source creation/addition, value copy and release. A synthetic bundle/target replaces app dependencies. Inject store-create NULL: notification registration, source creation and AddSource each receive NULL once; release receives NULL twice across initialisation/deallocation. Inject source-create NULL with valid store: AddSource and release each receive NULL once; the valid store releases once. Healthy control: no NULL boundary calls and both created handles release once. No real SystemConfiguration access, run-loop mutation, DNS query, NULL release or crash occurs. Exact commands, source/SDK hashes and logs are retained locally.

**Impact and contracts:** These normal failure returns can prevent app startup instead of yielding an empty DNS-monitor state. Apple's [dynamic-store creator](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/systemconfiguration/scdynamicstorecreate(_:_:_:_:)) and SDK 27 declarations allow NULL results; its run-loop-source creator is nullable as well. Apple explicitly requires a non-NULL argument for [CFRelease](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/corefoundation/cfrelease) and documents an application crash otherwise. The proof measures the invalid arguments; native SystemConfiguration failure frequency, exact first crashing API and a real crash remain untested. No claim is made that DNS lookup itself is broken under healthy setup.

**Deduplication:** BACKEND-14/#35 involves an already-created reachability handle released twice after callback/scheduling failure. This issue involves unchecked creator NULL in a different app-wide DNS watcher, a startup path executed independently of account reachability, and requires initialisation guards plus an unavailable-watcher state.

**Future fix and regressions:** Check both creator results and notification registration before further use, release only live owned handles, and propagate a safe unavailable watcher/empty DNS list. Decide whether later watcher retry is appropriate without stopping otherwise usable app features. Test store-create failure, source-create failure, notification registration failure and healthy setup with inert boundaries. Assert no API receives a NULL required handle, valid handles release once, and the disabled DNS SRV/default startup path remains usable when the watcher cannot initialise.

**Limits:** Production Objective-C control flow and boundary arguments are measured. Real application startup, SystemConfiguration daemon/resource failures, native crash, DNS/provider state and user profile are untested. No credentials, personal data, visible UI or repository edits were involved.

issues.title: Keep calls controllable when a local hang-up request is rejected
issues.evidence: Released controller methods with inert rejected/accepted operation boundaries; exact SDK failure route source-traced
issues.body:
**Priority:** P2. **Confidence:** high for the measured controller state and source-confirmed SDK failure path. Actual native lock contention, provider calls, visible windows and ongoing audio were not exercised.

A failed local hang-up request can leave a confirmed call active while Telephone reports **call ended**, detaches its call-state delegate and disables the controls that could retry the operation. Closing the ended card then removes its controller without another hang-up request.

**Frozen source:** jps Telephone 2.1.8/build 160, `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`. [Telephone/CallController.m:343–374](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallController.m#L343-L374) clears `callActive`, stops recording and the timer, detaches the call delegate, invokes a void hang-up wrapper, and unconditionally presents the ended state. [Telephone/AKSIPCall.m:241–251](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPCall.m#L241-L251) checks the native status but only logs failure; it cannot communicate failure to its caller. The window-close path repeats this ordering ([Telephone/CallController.m:712–731](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallController.m#L712-L731)), while [Telephone/AccountController.m:871–874](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AccountController.m#L871-L874) removes closed controllers from account ownership. Delegate detachment removes its per-call state subscriptions ([Telephone/AKSIPCall.m:58–133](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPCall.m#L58-L133)).

**Reachable native failure, source only:** PJSIP 2.17 `acquire_call` returns `PJ_ETIMEDOUT` when the SDK or dialog mutex cannot be acquired within its configured limit. `pjsua_call_hangup` returns that error before setting `hanging_up`, deinitialising media or emitting its disconnect callback. The vendored header has a 2000 ms default and no local override. This is a failure to accept the local operation; successful background signalling completion is a separate SDK state. The [official 2.17 call API](https://docs.pjsip.org/en/2.17/api/generated/pjsip/group/group__PJSUA__LIB__CALL.html) documents a result status for hang-up. See [PJSIP's 2.17 source](https://github.com/pjsip/pjproject/blob/2.17/pjsip/src/pjsua-lib/pjsua_call.c); the saved source in `outputs/audit-2.1.8/sip/pjsua_call.c` has `acquire_call` at 2405–2475 and the early hang-up return at 3245–3247. No native operation was executed to force this timeout.

**Measured component evidence:** `SDKReturnStateProbe.m` executes the exact existing Release `CallController.hangUpCall`, `windowWillClose:`, `setCallActive:` and state getters on actual subclasses allocated without initializers. Fake calls deliberately reject at the request boundary and remain active/Confirmed. Presentation, recording, notification, defaults and delayed-close collaborators are counters. All 66 assertions across eight hang-up/transfer scenarios pass. The relevant source files match the frozen compiled source byte for byte; source/object hashes and compile/link commands are in `state-provenance.json`.

For rejected hang-up, `state-results.json` records native-boundary active=true/state=5, actual controller active=false, delegateRetained=false, timerStops=1, recordStops=1, status="call ended", endedShows=1, hangUpDisallows=1, accept/decline disabled and notificationRemovals=1. With auto-close true, the production method schedules one close. The actual close handler records owner closure while the fake call remains active, and its request count stays one because the controller was already marked inactive. Direct window closure while active also drops ownership after the rejected request. The accepted boundary control becomes inactive/Disconnected and receives the same ended presentation. These counters prove requested presentation and state changes; they do not show a real window, measure call duration/end time, stop real recording, or establish continued peer audio.

**Impact:** There is no retained controller call-state subscription or enabled hang-up control for this still-active call. A real mutex timeout before native hang-up would leave its media/session untouched at that point, so ongoing connection/audio is a source-supported consequence, not a runtime measurement. Auto-close and manual close can remove the controller. Actual frequency and duration are unmeasured.

**Future fix:** Return or complete with a result from `AKSIPCall.hangUp`. Commit ended state and detach ownership only after accepted native termination or observed disconnect. On local failure, retain the delegate, active state and retry controls, present an error, and keep any explicit close operation from silently orphaning the call. Treat an already-disconnected native session idempotently; preserve successful asynchronous hang-up semantics.

**Regression expectations:** Reject local hang-up while keeping a confirmed boundary call active; assert it remains controllable and subscribed, with no final-ended presentation or auto-close. Repeat with direct close and subsequent retry. Include accepted termination, already-disconnected sessions and delayed native disconnect. Verify that recording and timers follow actual termination, rather than a rejected attempt.

**Deduplication:** Distinct from #17/BACKEND-07 SDK-lock UI blocking: this is the incorrect state after an SDK error, not the time spent waiting. Distinct from #21/SIP-04: no successful transfer or transfer-result lifetime is involved. Existing issues #2–39 were checked; no prior issue describes rejected local hang-up restoration.

**Boundary:** No production application/controller/account/agent/view initializer, NSApplication, window, nib, provider, network endpoint, native SDK call, URI/protocol payload, profile, defaults, Keychain, Contacts or audio/hardware access. Initializer-free production-layout receivers are retained until process exit and their cleanup is not executed. Full Release-object linkage resolves symbols only.

issues.title: Restore Transfer after the preliminary local hold request is rejected
issues.evidence: Released controller methods with inert rejected/accepted operation boundaries; exact SDK failure route source-traced
issues.body:
**Priority:** P2. **Confidence:** high for the measured transfer-action latch and source-confirmed immediate SDK failure paths. Native hold negotiation, provider calls and visible transfer-sheet behaviour were not exercised.

An attended transfer can remain disabled when its preliminary local hold request fails. The transfer action disables **Transfer** and waits for a hold callback even though the SDK rejected that operation, so the transfer request is never made and the action has no local recovery path.

**Frozen source:** jps Telephone 2.1.8/build 160, `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`. [Telephone/ActiveCallTransferViewController.m:42–56](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/ActiveCallTransferViewController.m#L42-L56) calls `toggleCallHold`, disables Transfer and sets `waitingForHold=YES` when the destination consultation call is not yet held. [Telephone/CallController.m:426–429](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallController.m#L426-L429) forwards the action through a void API. [Telephone/AKSIPCall.m:360–380](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPCall.m#L360-L380) checks `pjsua_call_set_hold` only to disconnect a recorder on success, and does not propagate a failed status. `callDidHold` is the path that clears the waiting flag and initiates the transfer. The destination controller invokes it only from its hold notification ([Telephone/CallTransferController.m:192–195](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallTransferController.m#L192-L195)). Transfer can otherwise be enabled by a later confirmation/active-media notification ([Telephone/CallTransferController.m:175–189](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallTransferController.m#L175-L189)); immediate rejection supplies no promised new notification, so that unrelated recovery is not assured.

**Reachable native failures, source only:** PJSIP 2.17 `pjsua_call_set_hold2` returns an acquisition error before making the hold request, and returns a failed re-INVITE creation status before it sets `local_hold`. A pending INVITE transaction causes `pjsip_inv_reinvite` to return `PJ_EINVALIDOP`, so an existing confirmed call with another negotiation in progress is one source-confirmed local rejection. Acquisition timeout is another. The [official 2.17 call API](https://docs.pjsip.org/en/2.17/api/generated/pjsip/group/group__PJSUA__LIB__CALL.html) specifies a result status for hold and reports hold changes through media callbacks. [PJSIP's 2.17 call source](https://github.com/pjsip/pjproject/blob/2.17/pjsip/src/pjsua-lib/pjsua_call.c) corresponds to saved `pjsua_call.c`:3384–3386,3428–3431,3448–3457. [PJSIP's INVITE source](https://github.com/pjsip/pjproject/blob/2.17/pjsip/src/pjsip-ua/sip_inv.c) contains the pending-transaction return in `pjsip_inv_reinvite`. No transaction, request or payload was constructed in the probe.

**Measured component evidence:** `SDKReturnStateProbe.m` executes exact existing Release `ActiveCallTransferViewController.transferCall:`, `callDidHold`, `disallowTransfer`, `CallController.toggleCallHold` and released hold-state accessors on actual subclasses allocated without initializers. Fake calls reject/no-op at the request boundary. A private inert button records the enabled state; transfer invocation is a counter. All 66 assertions across eight hang-up/transfer scenarios pass. Source/object hashes, frozen-build source equality and compile/link commands are in `state-provenance.json`.

For rejected hold, `state-results.json` records one hold request, native-boundary localHold=false, actual controller callOnHold=false, waitingForHold=true, transferEnabled=false and transferRequests=0. With no hold acknowledgement, state remains unchanged. The accepted boundary control has waiting=true/Transfer disabled until the separate inert hold acknowledgement reaches the actual `callDidHold`; that handler then clears waiting and issues exactly one transfer. An already-held control issues one transfer immediately without another hold request. A guard control shows the same pending latch when `CallController.toggleCallHold` makes no request because the call has remote hold; ordinary remote-hold UI disables Transfer separately, so this is a stale-action/control contract check rather than a claimed live trigger.

**Impact:** A failed preliminary hold blocks retry in the current transfer action until another suitable media/confirmation event or a reset of the transfer flow occurs. The measured result is the model/operation/button state. Actual UI rendering, provider behaviour and failure frequency are untested.

**Future fix:** Propagate immediate hold acceptance/failure through `AKSIPCall` and `CallController`. Enter waiting state only for accepted requests, and reset/re-enable eligible controls with an error when the request is rejected or deferred negotiation fails. Guard actions against a newer call state, associate acknowledgements with the pending operation, and preserve the already-held path without toggling an unrelated/manual hold.

**Regression expectations:** Reject the preliminary hold while consultation remains confirmed/unheld; assert waiting=false, Transfer can retry and no transfer is sent. Include an already-held call, accepted hold followed by acknowledgement, a state change before action dispatch, disconnect while pending, and later media notifications so stale callbacks cannot transfer the wrong call. Cover local `PJ_EINVALIDOP`/timeout boundaries separately from provider rejection.

**Deduplication:** Distinct from #31/GUI-11: this starts with an unheld consultation call and a failed Transfer action; that issue closes setup and changes a previously manually held source call. Distinct from #21/SIP-04: no successful transfer result is produced or discarded. Existing issues #2–39 were checked; no prior issue describes restoring the failed preliminary-hold action.

**Boundary:** No production application/controller/account/agent/view initializer, NSApplication, window, nib, provider, network endpoint, native SDK call, URI/protocol payload, profile, defaults, Keychain, Contacts or audio/hardware access. Initializer-free production-layout receivers are retained until process exit and their cleanup is not executed. Full Release-object linkage resolves symbols only.

issues.title: Validate existing account edits before re-enabling and overwriting saved values
issues.evidence: 38 assertions over exact released Enable action with only in-memory settings/control/notification/Keychain request counters; normal account creation source-traced
issues.body:
**Priority: P2. Confidence: high for the measured saved-data and control-state mutation. Native account creation/registration is source-traced, not exercised.**

Re-enabling an existing account can replace its previously saved Domain or Username with an empty value, persist the account as enabled, and lock the fields against editing. The user must disable it again and reconstruct the deleted value. This is a commit-boundary validation failure in the existing-account editor, distinct from first setup and authentication sheets.

**Frozen source:** 2.1.8/build 160, `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`.

- [AccountPreferencesViewController.m:435–469](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AccountPreferencesViewController.m#L435-L469): trims Domain/Username and copies both into the saved dictionary without testing either for emptiness.
- [AccountPreferencesViewController.m:547–568](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AccountPreferencesViewController.m#L547-L568): disables all editable account fields after Enable.
- [AccountPreferencesViewController.m:573–613](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AccountPreferencesViewController.m#L573-L613): Disable exposes the fields, and either branch writes the new dictionary and sends the enabled-change notification.
- [AppController.m:405–420](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AppController.m#L405-L420): the enable notification creates a replacement enabled controller from the saved values.

**Normal trigger:** Open Settings → Accounts for an existing account, uncheck Enable, clear Domain or Username (or enter only spaces/newlines), and check Enable. Both controls are editable while disabled and Enable remains available. There is no requirement to edit a file, create malformed external input or authenticate to a server.

**Measured evidence:** `AccountEditProbe.m` invokes the exact released `changeAccountEnabled:` method on an actual subclass allocated without an initializer. All fields are inert NSObject recorders. `standardUserDefaults`, notification-center and Keychain entry points are replaced inside the disposable process by in-memory recorders before invocation; address-label allocation is also replaced, so no URI is constructed or parsed. No real defaults domain or Keychain item is accessed. Four cases—valid values, empty Domain, empty Username, and whitespace-only values in both fields—pass **38 assertions**.

Every invalid case makes one saved-data write with `AccountEnabled=true`, replaces the affected old valid value with an empty string, disables Domain/Username, reloads the account table and sends one enabled-change notification. The whitespace-only case stores both as empty. The valid control saves its nonempty new values. Keychain helpers are inert request counters and are never executed; the fake password remains unchanged so there is no save request. Results and exact source/object hashes, compile/link commands and boundaries are in `results.json` and `provenance.json`.

**Downstream trace and limits:** `AKSIPAccount.initWithDictionary:parser:` at 228–278 asserts key presence rather than nonempty values and retains the new strings. `AKSIPUserAgent.addAccount:withPassword:` at 729–733 returns NO on native add failure but does not roll back Settings. `AccountController.setAccountRegistered:` at 104–116 shows Connecting before add and its following error branch is conditional on add success. PJSIP's [2.17 account API](https://docs.pjsip.org/en/2.17/api/generated/pjsip/group/group__PJSUA__LIB__ACC.html) documents a status return from account add; rejection cannot undo an earlier application preference write. No native account, endpoint, provider registration, real window, crash or audio consequence was tested or is claimed. An explicit advanced account address/registrar may make an empty Domain tolerated by some configurations; that does not change the measured unvalidated overwrite of the user's previously saved values. Validate the product's supported required/override combinations rather than inventing a universal protocol constraint.

**Future fix:** Validate trimmed required fields at the Enable commit boundary, including any explicitly supported address/registrar override combinations. On failure, keep the account disabled and editable, retain the previous saved account, focus the invalid field and display a useful error. Do not read/write Keychain or notify/recreate the enabled account until this validation succeeds. Apple's [NSControlTextEditingDelegate](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nscontroltexteditingdelegate?language=objc) offers editing-time validation; the Enable action also needs a final authoritative check because it commits multiple fields together.

**Regression expectations:** Start with a valid disabled in-memory saved account; reject empty and whitespace-only required values without any saved-data or Keychain mutation, enable notification or locked fields. Include valid edited values and supported explicit address/registrar configurations. Verify Disable itself still enables editing and that prior saved values survive a rejected Enable. Add a nib/action-level isolated test separately from native registration integration.

**Deduplication:** #18/GUI-07 concerns first-setup whitespace validation; #19/GUI-08 concerns authentication sheet dismissal/mutation. This path edits an existing saved account, overwrites its previous values, commits enabled state and locks editing. Existing Keychain persistence failure #16 is excluded; no Keychain failure is required for this finding.

**Boundary:** No application/account/agent/view initializer, actual NSUserDefaults instance or domain, Keychain operation, Contacts lookup, audio/hardware, endpoint, network, OS preference, visible UI or GitHub write. The linked production object code only resolves symbols. Receivers remain retained until the disposable process exits, avoiding production cleanup.

issues.title: Cancel pending outgoing calls when their account is removed
issues.evidence: 30 assertions over released outgoing request/captured completion/model ownership with inert native boundary; PJSIP forced-delete contract source-traced
issues.body:
**Priority: P2. Confidence: high for the measured late model attachment; native request/account-deletion interleaving and peer effects are source-supported, not live-tested.**

An outgoing request whose account is removed before its queued success completion reaches the main thread can still create and return a Calling model for that removed account. The completion only validates the whole user-agent instance. It does not validate the account's membership, native identifier or cancellation intent.

**Frozen source:** jps Telephone 2.1.8/build 160, `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`.

- [AKSIPAccount.m:302–322](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPAccount.m#L302-L322): captures the account/native identifier for an asynchronous make request. Its success completion unconditionally calls `addCallWithInfo:`.
- [AKSIPAccount.m:325–367](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPAccount.m#L325-L367): captures successful native info, then schedules main-thread completion. It checks started state and the user-agent audio generation, with no per-account validity check.
- [AKSIPAccount.m:372–395](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPAccount.m#L372-L395): missing models are created from the saved snapshot; prior removal provides no cancellation/terminal guard.
- [AppController.m:421–435](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AppController.m#L421-L435): disabling an account closes its cards and removes the account while keeping the overall user agent running.
- [CallController.m:712–731](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallController.m#L712-L731): a pending new card is not yet callActive, so closing it skips native hangup and notifies its owner.
- [AKSIPUserAgent.m:748–758](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L748-L758): removes existing model calls, deletes the native account, removes its registry entry and invalidates its identifier, without changing the outgoing request's generation token.
- [AccountController.m:357–366](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AccountController.m#L357-L366): the higher-level success completion attaches the returned call and marks the captured card active without checking whether it was closed or its account was disabled.

**Normal trigger:** Begin an outgoing call, then disable/remove that account in Settings while the local make request or its main-thread completion is pending. A safe bounded ordering is: native make/get-info succeeds; its result is captured; an account-disable action is in progress on main and closes the pending card/removes the account; the saved completion then runs while the same user agent is still started. No account identifier reuse or malicious input is required.

**Exact local component proof:** `OutboundOwnershipProbe.m` executes released `AKSIPAccount.makeCallTo:completion:`, its actual captured completion block, model add/lookup/remove methods, identifier update, and the real `AKSIPCall` initializer/state storage. The account is an initializer-free subclass; an inert agent accepts queueing and supplies a constant generation. The actual worker selector is intercepted before execution, and URI allocation returns label-only NSObject collaborators, so no URI is serialised/parsed and no native SDK request occurs. Native success/failure is an explicitly inert completion argument. Models/receivers remain retained until process exit, avoiding production cleanup.

**30 assertions pass across four scenarios:**

- Current account + accepted completion: one model returned, Calling state, identifier remains 3.
- Removed account + accepted saved completion: account identifier is -1, generation remains 7, yet one new Calling model is added and returned. Its queued parameters still carry former native account identifier 3.
- Removed account + rejected completion: no model and nil result (negative control).
- A model marked Disconnected and removed before an accepted older snapshot: the completion adds a Calling model again. This control demonstrates the lack of a terminal/cancellation check at this boundary; a separate real SDK disconnect-ordering race is not claimed.

The source file matches the frozen local Release build byte for byte. Results, object/source hashes and compile/link commands are in `results.json` and `provenance.json`. No visible card, native call, provider, registration, peer audio or packet was observed.

**SDK ownership contract:** PJSIP's [2.17 account API](https://docs.pjsip.org/en/2.17/api/generated/pjsip/group/group__PJSUA__LIB__ACC.html) permits forced account deletion with active calls. The [official 2.17 source](https://github.com/pjsip/pjproject/blob/2.17/pjsip/src/pjsua-lib/pjsua_acc.c#L756-L884) shows `pjsua_acc_del` setting force=true; `pjsua_acc_del2` warns about active/async dialogs and proceeds with account cleanup without terminating those calls. Its concluding comment says calls should have been terminated first unless forced. The matching saved reference is `outputs/audit-2.1.8/sip/pjsua_acc.c:756–884`; vendored `pj/config.h:1671–1683` identifies 2.17. Therefore deleting the native account is not an implicit cancellation of the accepted outgoing call. These SDK semantics are source/documentation evidence, not a forced native deletion experiment.

**Impact and limits:** Account removal can be followed by a model attachment to an invalid/removed account and to a card whose normal owner already released it. Subsequent normal agent lookup cannot find that removed account's calls. A surviving native call can become unmanaged by this registry, but actual peer/media continuation is not measured. The success handler does not call showWindow, so this finding does **not** claim visible window resurrection. The retained stale-state/model and cancelled ownership boundary are the proven application defect; failure frequency is unknown.

**Future fix:** Associate every outgoing operation with the account's current lifetime/cancellation token, not just the user-agent generation. Invalidate and drain pending operations when an account or card is disabled/removed. Reject late model/controller attachment; if a native request was already accepted, terminate that exact dialog safely rather than silently discarding its result or using a reused numeric slot. Account removal should preserve callback ownership until accepted calls are cancelled/disconnected. Keep current successful requests and ordinary user-agent restart cancellation intact.

**Regression expectations:** Pause completion of an accepted make request, remove/disable its account and close its pending card, then release the result. Assert no model is attached to the removed account/card and that the accepted native dialog receives an explicit cancellation/ownership handoff at an inert backend boundary. Include accepted current, rejected removed, account re-enable/replacement, user-agent restart, and an already disconnected snapshot; verify stale identifiers cannot terminate a newer call. Actual provider tests should be separate.

**Deduplication:** #23/SIP-06 is a late incoming callback with a removed account and invalid notification delivery. This finding concerns an outgoing operation captured earlier and unconditionally accepted later. #40/SIP-09 starts with an attached active call and a rejected hangup; here the pending card has no attached active call and makes no hangup request. #27/SIP-07 concerns delayed registration intent, not outgoing model ownership. No existing issue covers this account-scoped outgoing cancellation boundary.

**Boundary:** Local disposable executable only; no normal application/controller/agent/view initialization, native SDK operation, endpoint/network/protocol payload, profile/defaults, credentials/Keychain, Contacts, audio/hardware, OS preference/event or UI. Repository remains unchanged; root owns issue publication.

issues.title: Preserve active-call callback ownership when an account goes Offline
issues.evidence: 64 assertions over released Offline/model lookup/ownership with inert native account removal and independent 39-assertion callback controls; native survival source-supported only
issues.body:
SIP-12 — Preserve active-call callback ownership when an account goes Offline

Priority P2. High confidence for the measured model ownership/lookup contract; native call survival and subsequent notification loss are supported by the frozen application and PJSIP 2.17 source, with no peer, provider or audio execution.

In jps Telephone 2.1.8/build 160 at `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`, selecting **Offline** for an account with an already-confirmed call removes that call from the application's callback registry while the existing call controller retains it and remains active. Later call-state and media callbacks cannot locate the retained call. This is a stable existing-call trigger; no pending outgoing completion or reused identifier is required.

The account menu forwards Offline without an active-call guard ([AccountWindowController.m:296–303](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AccountWindowController.m#L296-L303)). The released selection method calls account removal ([AccountController.m:418–424](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AccountController.m#L418-L424)); that removal only invalidates its timer, requests Offline presentation and calls the user agent ([AccountController.m:249–254](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AccountController.m#L249-L254)). It does not hang up the existing call controllers.

The actual user-agent removal path clears `account.calls` before calling `pjsua_acc_del`, then removes the account from `userAgent.accounts` and invalidates its account identifier on success ([AKSIPUserAgent.m:742–760](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L742-L760)). `removeAllCalls` empties the model collection ([AKSIPAccount.m:394–396](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPAccount.m#L394-L396)), and global call lookup only searches that collection through currently registered application accounts ([AKSIPUserAgent.m:773–781](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L773-L781)). The account controller's `callControllers` ownership is unchanged on this route.

Native survival is source-only. The vendored [PJSIP account contract](https://docs.pjsip.org/en/2.17/api/generated/pjsip/group/group__PJSUA__LIB__ACC.html) and `ThirdParty/PJSIP/include/pjsua-lib/pjsua.h:5277–5311` specify that `pjsua_acc_del` forces account deletion regardless of active calls. In official [PJSIP 2.17 source](https://github.com/pjsip/pjproject/blob/2.17/pjsip/src/pjsua-lib/pjsua_acc.c), `pjsua_acc_del:756–761` sets `force=TRUE`; `pjsua_acc_del2:782–801` permits an existing INVITE/dialog in that mode. The remaining cleanup through its success return at 884 contains no active-call termination. The comment at 867–869 says calls should ordinarily have been terminated before account deletion. Those lines refer to the saved official source `outputs/audit-2.1.8/sip/pjsua_acc.c`, not an exercised native operation.

Once the model is absent, the queued call-state body drops a non-Calling snapshot before updating the call or posting a notification ([PJSUAOnCallState.m:88–104](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/PJSUAOnCallState.m#L88-L104)). Its disconnect handling and event emission therefore do not run ([115–118](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/PJSUAOnCallState.m#L115-L118)). The media callback likewise returns on the missing model ([PJSUAOnCallMediaState.m:52–58](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/PJSUAOnCallMediaState.m#L52-L58)). A later peer disconnect cannot reach the controller's normal inactive/timer/recording cleanup through that routing ([CallController.m:792–795](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallController.m#L792-L795)). Stale active presentation, missing disconnect history/ringtone fan-out, and delayed recording cleanup are source-supported consequences; no real window, history or recording effect was measured.

`OfflineRegistryProbe.m` invokes the exact existing Release `AccountController.changeAccountState`, `removeAccountFromUserAgent` and `SIPAccountWillRemove` methods, the actual account registry removal/query/update methods, the actual global account/call lookup methods, and `CallController.callActive` setter/getter. Actual subclasses are allocated with their inherited layout, without any initializer. The user-agent removal override is an inert successful-removal boundary: it applies actual `account.removeAllCalls` and application collection mutations without invoking the real native removal method. The fake call remains Confirmed/active and counts any hang-up request.

All **64 assertions across three scenarios pass**:

- Offline: account call registry 1→0; account identifier 0→−1; global call lookup true→false, already false immediately after clearing the call registry. The controller is still owned, still retains its call, remains active, and its call delegate stays attached. The boundary call remains state 5/active with zero hang-up requests.
- Unavailable negative control: one inert unregister request; call/account lookups and registry remain intact, and the controller stays active.
- Another-account control: Offline removes only the selected account; the other account's call remains findable.

The separate round-02 production-callback control executes the exact existing `PJSUAOnCallState.o` with inert native info/model/parser collaborators. Its Confirmed snapshot with no model emits zero events. Its repeated-disconnect control emits one event for the first callback, removes its model, then emits no additional event for the second callback. This is independent callback evidence from the 39-assertion suite, **not one end-to-end Offline-to-native-disconnect fixture**.
