The Offline fixture does not invoke a PJSUA callback or measure delivered notifications.

Results, commands and matching frozen source/object hashes are in `offline-registry-results.json` and `offline-registry-provenance.json`; the callback control is `../round-02/state-guard-results.json`, `state-guard-provenance.json`, and `state_guard_probe.m`. Reproduce the Offline component check with `python3 run_offline_registry_probe.py` from this directory. No production application/controller/account/agent/view initializer, native SDK operation, endpoint, URI/protocol payload, provider, profile, defaults, Keychain, Contacts, real audio/UI or OS action is executed. Production-layout receivers are retained through `_Exit` so their cleanup is not run. Full Release linkage resolves symbols only.

Future fix: preserve active calls and their callback routing independently of registration/account-menu state. If Offline is intended to leave current calls connected, retain the native/model account lifecycle or a dedicated active-call registry until each call disconnects. If Offline should terminate calls, explicitly request termination and preserve routing until accepted termination/disconnect, then delete the account. Do not clear the registry while an existing native call can still report state or media changes.

Regression expectations: start with an already-confirmed call, select Offline, and then deliver hold/media/remote-disconnect acknowledgements. Each surviving call must still resolve by native ID and receive the corresponding state/cleanup events, or be explicitly terminated before registry removal according to the chosen product policy. Include incoming/outgoing calls, multiple calls/accounts, Unavailable, returning Available, account deletion/disable, and queued callbacks. Provider integration can be separate from inert model-routing tests.

Distinct from SIP-11's pending asynchronous make completion, #23/SIP-06's late incoming callback/nil notification, #27/SIP-07's startup Offline intent, #32/SIP-08's manual Unavailable policy, and #40/SIP-09's rejected hang-up: this starts with an existing confirmed controller and requests no hang-up. Posted #2–43 and all supplied SIP exclusions were checked. No issue filed by this subagent.

issues.title: Apply saved Network configuration changes made during user-agent startup
issues.evidence: 32 assertions/four state controls over released Network settings/restart/start-completion handlers with inert settings and copied configuration boundary; native stale settings source-traced
issues.body:
**Priority: P2. Confidence: high for the measured application restart/defer omission; stale native configuration is a bounded source-supported consequence, not a native startup measurement.**

Saving app-wide Network changes while the user agent is Starting can leave the newly started instance using its previous configuration. The Save action writes preferences and promises immediate application/reconnection, but the app requests restart only when the agent is already Started. If the worker has already copied the old values, neither Save nor successful-start completion schedules the required restart.

**Frozen source:** jps Telephone 2.1.8/build 160, `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`.

- [NetworkPreferencesViewController.m:121–133](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/NetworkPreferencesViewController.m#L121-L133): Save confirmation states that changes apply immediately and accounts reconnect.
- [NetworkPreferencesViewController.m:141–174](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/NetworkPreferencesViewController.m#L141-L174): persists fields and posts the changed-settings notification with no Starting guard or deferred application.
- [AppController.m:458–480](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AppController.m#L458-L480): updates the agent's configuration properties but requests restart only when isStarted is true.
- [AKSIPUserAgent.m:382–443](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L382-L443): the control thread copies name-server/proxy/STUN/ICE/port values into native configuration structs, then initialises the SDK. Transports are subsequently created using the copied transport config.
- [AKSIPUserAgent.m:569–582](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L569-L582): native startup completes before its completion is queued on main.
- [AppController.m:503–522](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AppController.m#L503-L522): success has no config revision comparison or deferred restart; it clears the generic pending-restart flag.

**Normal bounded trigger:** Open Network settings, change an app-wide value such as ICE or the transport port, and Save while a registration-triggered startup is still in progress. In the relevant ordering, the worker has consumed the old configuration (or completed native startup), but the queued main-thread completion has not yet changed the application agent state to Started. A Settings sheet/action can run before that completion. The fields/Save path are not disabled while Starting; their only startup observer updates a port placeholder. Saving before the worker reads the fields is a different, potentially successful ordering and is not the bug.

**Measured local proof:** `NetworkStartProbe.m` executes exact released `AppController.preferencesControllerDidChangeNetworkSettings:`, `restartUserAgent` and `SIPUserAgentDidFinishStarting:` on an actual subclass allocated without an initializer. All settings live in an NSObject recorder substituted for the process's standard-defaults getter. Configuration, account collection, stop request and startup acknowledgement are inert collaborators. The old already-consumed configuration is explicitly a **test-double copy**, not an SDK snapshot. No actual preferences or native startup occur.

**32 assertions pass across four state controls:**

- Starting + Apply: requested port/ICE properties change, but stop/restart requests remain zero and no register-after-restart flag is established.
- The same case + inert successful-start acknowledgement through the real released handler: no restart or account re-registration is requested, and the pending-restart flag is false. The old consumed copy remains unchanged.
- Started + Apply: the actual restart helper makes one stop request and records that accounts should register after restart (positive control).
- Stopped/Stopping + Apply: properties are updated without an immediate stop; these controls establish that the missing action is specifically consequential when an in-flight startup has already consumed the earlier values. They do not claim another defect in these states.

Results, source/object hashes and compile/link commands are in `results.json` and `provenance.json`. The source matches the frozen local Release build. The proof measures the application's requested-property/restart/defer decisions. It does not measure native transport, ICE/STUN/DNS/proxy configuration, reconnection, actual settings UI or provider behaviour.

**Configuration contract:** PJSIP's [2.17 startup API](https://docs.pjsip.org/en/2.17/api/generated/pjsip/group/group__PJSUA__LIB__BASE.html) takes configuration structs at initialisation and separates that step from startup; transports are created separately. Telephone's property assignments after those local copies do not update already-initialised SDK settings or existing transports. The app's own normal Started save handler deliberately restarts, confirming its application-level contract. Consequently the above cut point permits successful startup with old values and no future application request. This is source reasoning, not a reproduced native timing race. The frequency/window duration is unmeasured.

**Impact:** A user can save valid network edits and see startup succeed while the active native instance continues with old settings until another restart. This can make connectivity troubleshooting and the stated all-account application behaviour unreliable. No native/provider failure, packet, security downgrade, crash or audio symptom is claimed.

**Future fix:** Track a configuration revision or explicit pending Network restart through Starting. Snapshot the desired settings for each startup; on completion, compare against the latest saved revision and perform a coordinated restart before treating that instance as current. Preserve the newer pending request rather than clearing it generically. Alternatively prevent/defer Save while Starting with a clear application contract. Maintain normal Started restarts and Stopped startup using the latest values; account registration should resume only on the chosen current configuration.

**Regression expectations:** Pause an inert worker after configuration consumption, deliver Save while application state is Starting, then release success/failure completion. Assert the new settings are applied through an explicit deferred restart/retry and old results cannot clear newer revision intent. Include Save before consumption, repeated saves, Started/Stopped/Stopping controls, termination, and no unrelated account/model mutations. Test native transport/config integration separately.

**Deduplication:** #27/SIP-07 loses a newer Offline registration intent during startup; this loses app-wide saved configuration application. #32/SIP-08 overwrites stable manual availability during automatic lifecycle registration. #36/BACKEND-15 concerns Sound device-query presentation. Existing immediate SDK hangup/hold failure and account-lifetime issues require no global Network save and are excluded.

**Boundary:** Local inert recorders and exact application handlers only. No real defaults/domain, application/agent/account/view initialization, normal/native startup/configuration, endpoint/network/protocol payload, Keychain/credentials, Contacts, audio/hardware, OS state/preference/event, visible UI or GitHub mutation. Repository source remains unchanged.

issues.title: Reset ringback bookkeeping when the SIP user agent restarts
issues.evidence: 32 assertions/four ringback flag/count/connection controls on released methods with inert conference boundary; restart and lost-disconnect chain source-traced
issues.body:
SIP-13 — Reset ringback bookkeeping when the SIP user agent restarts

Priority P2. High confidence for the measured ringback cache/connection-request contract. Shutdown ordering and the missing callback route are source-traced and separately component-supported. Actual sleep, native SDK teardown/start, peer replies and audible ringback were not exercised.

At frozen jps Telephone 2.1.8/build 160, `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`, stopping and restarting SIP while a call is producing local ringback can leave its old `ringbackOn` flag and positive `ringbackCount` in the shared user-agent object. The new native SIP instance creates another tone port, but these stale values prevent a later ringing call from requesting the connection from that new port to sound output.

The ordinary source trigger is sleep during an outgoing call's locally generated 180 ringback. [PJSUAOnCallState.m:68–74,120–123](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/PJSUAOnCallState.m#L68-L74) requests local ringback for a qualifying reply. [AppController.m:815–818](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AppController.m#L815-L818) stops SIP and waits. Its stop path first hangs up controllers and removes accounts ([179–187](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AppController.m#L179-L187), [AccountControllers.m:129–135](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AccountControllers.m#L129-L135)). `hangUpCall` does not stop ringback directly ([CallController.m:343–369](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallController.m#L343-L369)). Account removal clears the call registry ([AKSIPUserAgent.m:748–758](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L748-L758)), so the accepted hang-up's queued disconnect callback cannot find the model when main resumes ([PJSUAOnCallState.m:87–104](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/PJSUAOnCallState.m#L87-L104)). Its `stopRingbackForCall` at 116 is skipped.

The singleton is reused ([AKSIPUserAgent.m:242–249](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L242-L249)). Native teardown removes/destroys the old tone port ([618–638](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L618-L638)), and startup creates and adds a new one ([456–495](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L456-L495)). Neither start, teardown nor `finishStopping:640–652` resets `ringbackCount` or `_callData[].ringbackOn`. Only [start/stop ringback:788–816](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L788-L816) change those values.

`startRingbackForCall` returns immediately for a reused flagged call slot at 790–792. For another unflagged slot, it requests a conference connection only when `ringbackCount == 0` at 797, then increments the count regardless. Stale positive count therefore prevents connection in either case. [PJSIP's 2.17 media contract](https://docs.pjsip.org/en/2.17/api/generated/pjsip/group/group__PJSUA__LIB__MEDIA.html) explains that removing a conference port removes its interconnections; creating a new tone port does not retain the old sound-output edge. Audio restoration at 899–923 uses the same `startRingbackForCall` guard, so it does not clear this cache.

`RingbackStateProbe.m` executes the exact existing Release `startRingbackForCall`, `stopRingbackForCall`, `callData` and ringback slot/count accessors on an initializer-free production-layout subclass. `connectAudioSource` records requests only. The old and new tone-port values 41/42 are inert markers, not SDK ports. The only `stopRingbackForCall` call uses an invalid port, so the native disconnect/rewind branch cannot execute. Actual SIP teardown/start is not invoked; source demonstrates its unchanged cache and the fixture supplies the resulting old-cache/new-port state.

All **32 assertions across four scenarios pass**:

- Old slot 0 establishes count 1, flag true and one old-port connection request. A new port marker plus that same flagged slot requests zero fresh connections.
- An unflagged slot 1 with the stale count likewise requests zero fresh connections; it sets its flag and increases count to 2.
- A clean count/flag state requests one connection to the fresh port.
- Calling the actual cache-clearing stop method with an invalid port clears count/flag; a later fresh-port start requests its connection correctly.

`offline-registry-results.json` separately measures account/model lookup loss after removal. Round-02's exact production callback controls separately show that a missing model receives no state event, including the second repeated disconnect. These support the lifecycle boundary but are not a single sleep-to-native-restart audio fixture. Actual audible loss is an inference from the missing required connection, and can persist until an event clears the stale cache; permanent silence for all future calls is not claimed.

Source/object hashes, compile/link commands and results are in `ringback-state-provenance.json` and `ringback-state-results.json`. Reproduce the component check with `python3 run_ringback_state_probe.py`. No application/account/controller/agent initializer, singleton, SDK operation, endpoint, protocol/URI fixture, provider, profile/defaults, Keychain, Contacts, hardware/audio, real UI or OS event is invoked. Receiver teardown is prevented by retention through `_Exit`; full Release linkage resolves symbols only.

Future fix: reset the user-agent instance's ringback flags/count when its conference port and SIP instance are torn down, before another startup can use them. Keep bookkeeping aligned with the current tone-port generation rather than relying exclusively on model callbacks that shutdown deliberately discards. Preserve normal concurrent ringback counting within a live instance.

Regression expectations: begin local ringback, stop/restart with disconnect delivery unable to resolve the removed model, and request ringback from the new tone port for both reused and new call slots. Verify one fresh output connection, correct per-slot flags/count and normal stop. Include several ringing calls, repeated restart, failed startup, normal media/disconnect cleanup and valid/invalid tone ports. Run any audible/provider/sleep integration separately.

Distinct from SIP-12: that issue loses callbacks for an existing confirmed call during Offline; this concerns old ringback cache state surviving a complete native restart and suppressing a new call's required connection. Distinct from #26/#34 audio failure/recovery and #29 incoming ringtone output: no device error or incoming ringtone configuration is required. Posted #2–45 and new SIP-11/12 were checked. No issue filed by this subagent.

issues.title: Rebind the cached transfer observer when its source card redials
issues.evidence: 48 assertions/five source-call replacement/cache/notification controls over released transfer methods with in-process A/B objects and inert recording/close counters
issues.body:
GUI-13 — Rebind the cached transfer observer when its source card redials

Priority P2. High confidence for the measured observer/state/close-request contract. Actual redial/transfer/provider traffic, consultation disconnect and visible sheet behaviour remain source-traced or untested.

At frozen jps Telephone 2.1.8/build 160, `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`, a call card caches its transfer controller. That controller observes transfer results for the source call model that existed when it was created. Redial reuses the same card with another call model, but the cached controller keeps its original notification sender filter. A correctly delivered final result for the current source call consequently does not update its transfer state or request the expected sheet closure.

A bounded user sequence, with automatic call-window closing disabled so the ended card remains available, is: open and close transfer setup for call A without starting a consultation, end A, redial from that retained card as call B, then use transfer for B. This does not require a reused native identifier or a source-disconnect race.

[CallController.m:182–186](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallController.m#L182-L186) creates the transfer controller once and returns the cached instance thereafter. [CallTransferController.m:46–68,71–80](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallTransferController.m#L46-L80) registers it with `object:sourceCallController.call`, using model A. The setter also short-circuits when the source controller itself is unchanged. Redial attaches call B to the same source card ([CallController.m:415–418](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallController.m#L415-L418)); its [setCall:164–178](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallController.m#L164-L178) updates the call delegate and views but never rebinds the existing transfer observer.

[Apple's selector-observer contract](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/notificationcenter/addobserver%28_%3Aselector%3Aname%3Aobject%3A%29) limits delivery to the registered sender when `object` is supplied. Therefore the current B result cannot reach [CallTransferController.m:206–216](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallTransferController.m#L206-L216), which sets `sourceCallTransferred` and closes an already-inactive consultation. The later consultation-disconnect path also gates closure on that flag ([180–184](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallTransferController.m#L180-L184)). Conversely, an old-A event still matches the cached filter after B becomes current.

`TransferBindingProbe.m` executes exact existing Release `CallController.setCall`/call accessors/cached-transfer getter and `CallTransferController.setSourceCallController`/final-result observer/state accessors. Actual subclasses use the correct inherited layout and no initializers. The existing transfer cache is seeded directly to avoid its lazy initializer. The source window and view ivars are nil; recording stop and `closeSheet` are inert counters. Sender objects A/B and final status-200 events are ordinary in-process Foundation notification data, not call models or native/provider results.

All **48 assertions across five scenarios pass**:

- Initial A binding: its final result sets `sourceCallTransferred=true` and records one close request for the inactive consultation control.
- Redial attachment B: the actual source setter changes the current call and delegate; the cache remains the same instance. B's correctly delivered local final event leaves the flag false and records zero close requests.
- Calling the binding setter again with the same source card still misses B because its owner-identity guard returns.
- A's local event still matches after B is current, sets the flag and records one close request, confirming the observer remains attached to the stale sender.
- Explicitly refreshing the local observer binding to B restores the flag and close request. This is a positive control, not a production fix or a claimed product path.

Results, matching frozen source/object hashes and commands are `transfer-binding-results.json` and `transfer-binding-provenance.json`. Reproduce the component check with `python3 run_transfer_binding_probe.py`. No actual redial URI, native transfer/callback, provider, SDK operation, endpoint, application/account/controller/view initializer, nib/window/sheet, profile/defaults, Keychain, Contacts, audio or OS operation is invoked. Production cleanup is skipped by retention through `_Exit`. The measured close request is not evidence that a real sheet closed or remained visible.

Future fix: treat the observed source call model as a separate lifetime from its reusable controller. Remove the observer from the exact old model, bind the current model whenever the source card changes call, and reset transfer-session state at that boundary. The same-controller guard must still notice a different call model; simply reusing the source-controller setter cannot currently refresh it.

Regression expectations: initialise transfer setup against A, replace the source card's call with B as redial does, and deliver final B results. Assert current B updates transfer state and performs the proper closure policy while an old A result cannot affect B's session. Include repeated source reuse, successful/failed/nonfinal results, already-ended versus active consultation, and cache creation before/after redial. Keep real provider/visible sheet tests separate.

Independent of #21/SIP-04: that issue drops a transfer result after the SDK removes the source model. This fixture intentionally supplies a correctly delivered current-B result; it is still excluded by the stale A sender filter. Repairing #21 alone cannot rebind the cached observer. Distinct from #31/GUI-11 pre-existing source hold cancellation and SIP-10 rejected preliminary hold. Posted #2–46 and new SIP-11/12/13 were checked. No issue filed by this subagent.

issues.title: Complete first-run launch state after the first account is added
issues.evidence: 40 assertions/four controls over released first-run wrapper/account-added/dispatch/drain handlers with inert accepted setup and opaque markers; initial no-account branch/external event forwarding source-traced
issues.body:
BACKEND-18 — Complete first-run launch state after the first account is added

Priority P2. High confidence for the measured application event/dispatch state. Real first-run startup, Apple event or Services delivery, account creation/registration and provider calling were not executed.

At jps Telephone 2.1.8/build 160, `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`, successfully adding the first account leaves the application's `finishedLaunching` flag false. Later external call requests continue replacing an in-memory pending destination instead of reaching the call dispatcher. The user has successfully left setup and can use the normal account window, but URL/Services calling remains stuck on the startup queue for the remainder of that app run.

**Bounded normal trigger:** launch with no saved accounts, complete valid first-account setup, then use an external call URL or Telephone's text Service. This is independent of invalid/whitespace setup and does not depend on asynchronous native SIP completion.

[AppController.m:624–637](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AppController.m#L624-L637) installs the first-run setup actions and returns after presenting setup. That return bypasses both the only launch queue drain at line 657 and the only `finishedLaunching=YES` assignment at line 660 ([654–660](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AppController.m#L654-L660)). AppKit does not call applicationDidFinishLaunching again when this setup window completes. [Apple's launch-delegate contract](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsapplicationdelegate/applicationdidfinishlaunching%28_%3A%29) describes an initialization callback before the first event, rather than a per-window completion event.

For valid fields, [AccountSetupController.m:101–114](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AccountSetupController.m#L101-L114) saves the account, closes setup and posts the account-added notification. [AppController.addAccountOnFirstLaunch:305–320](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AppController.m#L305-L320) calls that setup action and restores normal Preferences/setup button actions. Its account-added handler ([376–386](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AppController.m#L376-L386)) installs the new account controller, updates menus and requests registration. Neither path completes `finishedLaunching` or drains the pending destination. A case-insensitive whole-source search found no alternative assignment or drain call.

[The Apple-event and text-Service handlers:841–854](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AppController.m#L841-L854) both call `makeCallOrRememberDestination`. That method ([866–871](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AppController.m#L866-L871)) dispatches only when `finishedLaunching` is true. Otherwise it merely stores/replaces `destinationToCall`. [Apple's event-registration API](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/nsappleeventmanager/seteventhandler%28_%3Aandselector%3Aforeventclass%3Aandeventid%3A%29) delivers to the registered handler; there is no automatic second launch callback that can repair this app-specific guard. New requests after a normal restart take the existing-account launch path and can dispatch, but the prior in-memory pending destination is not persisted for that restart.

**Measured component evidence:** `FirstLaunchProbe.m` executes the exact existing Release `addAccountOnFirstLaunch`, `accountSetupControllerDidAddAccount`, `makeCallOrRememberDestination` and `makeCallAfterLaunchIfNeeded` methods on an initializer-free production-layout AppController subclass. Initial `finishedLaunching=false` is explicitly seeded from the source no-account early-return state. The setup `addAccount` collaborator is an inert accepted-add event boundary; all four field guards return one constant nonempty marker. No real account or credential values are supplied or read. Account/menu/button/window/registration and outgoing dispatch collaborators are counters. It does not execute applicationDidFinishLaunching or AccountSetupController's persistence/Keychain action.

All **40 assertions across four scenarios pass**:

- The actual first-run wrapper calls the accepted setup boundary once; the actual account-added handler adds one controller, requests one window and one registration, and updates menu/account info once. The actual wrapper restores Preferences to `showPreferencePanel:` and the default action to `addAccount:`. Nevertheless `finishedLaunching=false` and there are zero dispatches.
- Two subsequent local dispatch markers produce zero outgoing-dispatch invocations and leave only the second marker stored.
- A marker queued before the first account is added also remains stored after the successful wrapper/event path, with zero dispatches.
- With finished-launch state true, the same actual dispatch guard invokes the inert dispatcher twice. Explicitly invoking the existing queue-drain helper dispatches the stored marker once and clears it; this is a positive control, not a production path after first setup.

The actual URL/Service forwarding and no-account initial state are source-traced. The test markers are opaque Foundation strings, not URIs or protocol payloads. No Apple event, pasteboard, provider, network/native SIP operation, endpoint, account/application/controller initializer, real profile/defaults/credential/Keychain/Contacts, hardware/audio, visible UI or OS setting was used. Released objects are linked only for method implementation resolution; retained production-layout receivers exit without production cleanup. The probe is not evidence of a real call starting or failing.

Commands, source/object hashes and results are in `provenance.json` and `results.json`. Reproduce locally with the saved `run_first_launch_probe.py`; it validates byte equality to the frozen Release source before linking.

**Future fix:** complete the common launch-ready state after valid first-account creation, once the account collection and necessary dispatch collaborators are ready. Drain the pending destination exactly once through the same registration-aware dispatcher used by normal launch. Keep incomplete/invalid/cancelled setup from claiming readiness, and avoid duplicating launch-only tasks or losing later requests.

**Regression expectations:** start at the no-account setup branch, successfully add a valid account, and then deliver URL and Services requests to their real handlers with inert dispatch collaborators. Assert launch-ready state becomes true and each new request is forwarded; a pre-setup queued destination must be drained once. Include rejected/cancelled setup, two successive external requests, existing-account launch and app termination. Real Apple event/Services/provider integration is a separate acceptance check.

**Deduplication:** checked published #2–47, including #18 invalid-whitespace first-setup wrapper, #19 authentication validation, #43 pending native make completion and #45 Apply-during-Starting. This is a successful first-run application-ready transition, before any native outbound operation. No issue was filed by this subagent.

issues.title: Connect the ended-transfer Call Back button to its redial delay
issues.evidence: 88 exact-method assertions/four missing/wired control scenarios plus six frozen XML assertions; compiled nib and visible interaction not exercised
issues.body:
**Priority: P3. Confidence: high for the source wiring omission and measured inherited control behavior; compiled nib and visible interaction were not tested.**

An ended transfer consultation leaves its Call Back button enabled immediately, bypassing the one-second protection used by ordinary ended calls. The shared disconnect handler attempts to disable the inherited redialButton outlet, but EndedCallTransferView never connects that outlet to its actual button.

**Frozen source:** jps Telephone 2.1.8/build 160, `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`.

- [EndedCallTransferView.xib:9–29](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/Base.lproj/EndedCallTransferView.xib#L9-L29): owner connects only view. Button 4 is enabled, has Call Back purpose and sends redial:, but has no redialButton outlet connection.
- [EndedCallView.xib:9–14](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/Base.lproj/EndedCallView.xib#L9-L14): the ordinary ended-call resource explicitly connects its redialButton outlet.
- [CallController.m:828–841](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallController.m#L828-L841): shared disconnect handling deliberately disables that outlet to prevent an accidental immediate callback and schedules its one-second enable tick.
- [EndedCallViewController.m:72–78](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/EndedCallViewController.m#L72-L78): inherited redial action invokes the controller; the enable tick only writes to redialButton.
- [CallTransferController.m:150–157](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallTransferController.m#L150-L157): the transfer controller uses EndedCallTransferView.
- [CallTransferController.m:180–184](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/CallTransferController.m#L180-L184): the normal transfer disconnect route calls the shared superclass handling; an unsuccessful/not-yet-transferred consultation remains available rather than closing.

**Normal trigger:** A transfer destination call ends or fails while its consultation sheet remains open. Its ended view presents Call Back. The application intends a brief delay on ended-call redial controls; the transfer resource bypasses that protection. No earlier source-card redial or failed preliminary hold is required.

**Local proof and controls:** Six XML assertions verify the frozen transfer resource's missing outlet, action/initial enabled state, and the ordinary resource's explicit connection. Separately, TransferRedialDelayProbe.m links exact released methods for the shared disconnect callback, ordinary transfer dispatch through its superclass, and inherited enable tick. Actual controller subclasses are allocated with the production layout without initializers. View/control/defaults/call/recording/notification collaborators are inert NSObject recorders; no nib, NSButton or window is constructed.

The fixture seeds the source-established missing/wired outlet configurations explicitly; it does not measure a compiled nib instance. Foundation schedules the real timer, which is captured and immediately invalidated before any run-loop delivery. The actual released tick is then invoked directly as a bounded control.

All **88 method assertions across four scenarios**, plus the **six resource assertions**, pass:

- Missing transfer outlet, direct inherited callback: the represented visible-control recorder remains enabled with zero enabled writes immediately and after the actual tick.
- Missing transfer outlet, normal CallTransferController disconnect dispatch: the same result, establishing that its superclass route does not supply another disable.
- Wired transfer positive control: immediate enabled=false with one write; actual tick restores enabled=true with two total writes.
- Ordinary ended-resource wiring control: the same disable/enable sequence.

Every case schedules exactly one nonrepeating one-second timer for the correct ended controller and marks the call inactive. The wired transfer is a counterfactual fixture control, not a production fix. Results and matching source/resource/object hashes are in `outputs/audit-2.1.8/repeated/gui/supplemental-after-GUI13/transfer-redial-delay-results.json` and `transfer-redial-delay-provenance.json`; the runner is `run_transfer_redial_delay_probe.py`.

**Impact and limits:** The intended temporary redial guard cannot reach the transfer button. Accidental callbacks are a source-supported risk; no click, real redial, peer call, compiled nib, visible sheet or actual accidental call was observed. This is a low-priority consistency/protection defect, not evidence of automatic dialling.

**Future fix:** Connect the transfer ended-view redialButton outlet to its Call Back button, or provide an explicit equivalent delay mechanism. Preserve the existing one-second policy, action and all calling/transfer behavior.

**Regression expectations:** Instantiate the actual compiled ended-transfer nib under an isolated test owner and assert its redialButton is the action-bearing control. Deliver an inert consultation disconnect; verify the button stays disabled until the scheduled tick, then becomes enabled. Compare the ordinary ended view, initial/repeated consultation failures and successful-transfer sheet closure. Keep provider and visible interaction acceptance separate.

**Deduplication:** Checked published #2–48. #47/GUI-13 concerns a stale source-call notification filter after redial; this missing outlet affects a fresh consultation and does not require source reuse. #31/GUI-11 concerns held-source restoration on Close; #41/SIP-10 concerns a rejected preliminary hold. None covers the ended consultation's redial guard.

**Boundary:** Local source/XML and exact-method recorders only; no production initializer, compiled nib/UI/button/window, native SDK/provider/network/protocol payload, real account/profile/defaults/Keychain/Contacts/audio/hardware, OS preference or real user action. Receiver cleanup is prevented by retention through process exit. No tracked source change.

issues.title: Defer Sound codec changes until the media endpoint is ready
issues.evidence: 24 assertions/six readiness/state controls over released Sound action/codec setter/update method with inert enum counter; native endpoint misuse source-supported, no crash run
issues.body:
BACKEND-19 — Defer Sound codec changes until the media endpoint is ready

Priority P2. High confidence for the measured premature application query and exact PJSIP 2.17 source contract. A native null-endpoint failure is source-supported; no native query, crash, device operation or live startup race was executed.

At jps Telephone 2.1.8/build 160, `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`, changing “Use only G.711 codec” while the user agent is Starting can enumerate codecs before PJSUA has created its media endpoint. The action is enabled and directly invokes a setter that permits Starting, although that state is assigned before the background worker begins PJSUA creation/initialization. In the early interval the SDK query dereferences a media-endpoint member without a readiness guard. This exposes a local application-failure risk while changing a normal Sound preference during startup.

**Bounded trigger and application path:** leave Settings → Sound open, request user-agent startup/registration, and toggle the G.711 checkbox before its control worker has completed media initialization. [The Sound XIB:108–116](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/Base.lproj/SoundPreferencesView.xib#L108-L116) wires the enabled checkbox to `changeUseG711Only:`. [The action:90–92](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/SoundPreferencesViewController.m#L90-L92) immediately assigns `userAgent.usesG711Only`. [The setter:232–236](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L232-L236) calls `updateCodecs` on a changed value; [the update:963–970](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L963-L970) returns only for Stopped or Stopping, so Starting reaches `pjsua_enum_codecs`. No UI-disable, SDK-ready condition or serialization to the control worker protects this action.

[Agent start:323–329](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L323-L329) publishes Starting and schedules its worker asynchronously. The worker later executes [`pjsua_create`:351](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L351-L356) and [`pjsua_init`:441](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L440-L447). Thus “Starting” includes a real source-level interval before the media endpoint exists. The test uses that bounded state as a supplied condition; it does not measure how often a user encounters the interval.

**Exact SDK contract:** the [vendored 2.17 header:129–141](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/ThirdParty/PJSIP/include/pjsua-lib/pjsua.h#L129-L141) separates create from initialize. Official 2.17 [`pjsua_create`:956–1055](https://github.com/pjsip/pjproject/blob/2.17/pjsip/src/pjsua-lib/pjsua_core.c#L956-L1055) first zeroes global state through [init_data:53–57](https://github.com/pjsip/pjproject/blob/2.17/pjsip/src/pjsua-lib/pjsua_core.c#L53-L57) and creates the SIP endpoint, but not the media endpoint. [`pjsua_init`:1296–1299](https://github.com/pjsip/pjproject/blob/2.17/pjsip/src/pjsua-lib/pjsua_core.c#L1296-L1299) later calls the media subsystem; [media initialization:103–108](https://github.com/pjsip/pjproject/blob/2.17/pjsip/src/pjsua-lib/pjsua_media.c#L103-L108) creates `med_endpt`. [Codec enumeration:4679–4689](https://github.com/pjsip/pjproject/blob/2.17/pjsip/src/pjsua-lib/pjsua_media.c#L4679-L4689) directly gets its codec manager with no endpoint-readiness check. [The endpoint getter:217–219](https://github.com/pjsip/pjproject/blob/2.17/pjmedia/src/pjmedia/endpoint.c#L217-L219) returns `&endpt->codec_mgr`; [the structure:73–82](https://github.com/pjsip/pjproject/blob/2.17/pjmedia/src/pjmedia/endpoint.c#L73-L82) places that member after two pointers. With a null endpoint this is an invalid member address rather than a safe null manager. [Enumeration:399–408](https://github.com/pjsip/pjproject/blob/2.17/pjmedia/src/pjmedia/codec.c#L399-L408) checks only non-null manager/count/output pointers and then accesses `mgr->mutex`. The premature native call therefore does not have a safe ready-state fallback in this version. This conclusion is source analysis, not a reproduced native crash.

**Measured evidence:** `CodecStartProbe.m` executes the existing released Sound action, `AKSIPUserAgent.setUsesG711Only:` and `updateCodecs` implementations on initializer-free production-layout receivers. The checkbox/state and media-readiness values are inert doubles. `pjsua_enum_codecs` is replaced with a counter returning zero codecs, so no priority call executes. The entire PJSUA archive is omitted from linking; its unresolved native operations are deliberately uninvoked. The probe cannot execute the unsafe native endpoint path.

All **24 assertions across six scenarios pass**: Starting-before-ready changes the flag and makes one enumeration attempt, marked before-ready; Stopped and Stopping change the stored flag with zero attempts; unchanged Starting also makes zero attempts; Started-ready and ready-Starting each make one attempt without the before-ready marker. The latter is an important positive control for legitimate startup-time configuration. Source and original Release object hashes, commands, boundary details and results are saved in `provenance.json` and `results.json`. No actual endpoint/SDK query, normal application/controller initializer, provider/network traffic, real account/profile/defaults/credential/Keychain/Contacts, device/audio, UI or OS-state change was used. Receivers are retained until process exit without production cleanup.

**Future fix:** retain the user's requested codec policy immediately, but defer/serialize UI-originated SDK operations until media initialization is complete. Preserve the existing control-worker initial codec application at [568, before pjsua_start/Started completion](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L567-L579). Simply making the whole `updateCodecs` method require Started would skip that legitimate initial configuration. A separate worker-only ready helper or explicit media-ready lifecycle/generation boundary can apply the latest pending value safely and discard work for failed/replaced startup.

**Regression expectations:** exercise the actual checkbox/setter with an early-Starting enum recorder and assert no premature SDK operation; complete initialization and assert the latest pending codec policy is applied once through the ready path. Keep Stopped, Stopping, Started-ready, ready-Starting, unchanged-value, repeated-toggle and failed/restarted-startup controls. Native startup timing/provider/device acceptance remains a separate check.

**Deduplication:** reviewed published #2–49, particularly #45/BACKEND-17 (Network Apply during Starting leaves an older configuration active), #26/BACKEND-10 audio-refresh recovery and #46 ringback restart caches. This is a Sound action issuing a readiness-dependent SDK query before initialization, rather than persistence, stale configuration, audio discovery or ringback cache. No source fix or GitHub mutation was made by this audit agent.

issues.title: Release the wrapper's PJLIB reference after failed startup
issues.evidence: 36 outer-reference counter assertions/six released-method startup/stop controls; PJLIB reference and suppressed native finalization consequences independently source-supported, no native operation
issues.body:
BACKEND-20 — Release the wrapper's PJLIB reference after failed startup

Priority P3. High confidence for the released-method ownership imbalance and exact2.17 reference semantics. Native resource retention is source-traced; no real startup failure, allocation-growth measurement, retry crash or peer/audio effect was executed.

At jps Telephone 2.1.8/build 160, `9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25`, a failed user-agent startup can mark the agent Stopped without releasing the PJLIB reference acquired by the application's `start` wrapper. Calling Stop afterward cannot release it. A later successful start/stop also releases only its own cycle's reference, leaving earlier failures outstanding and preventing PJLIB's zero-reference global finalization for the remainder of that process.

**Bounded trigger:** the wrapper's initial `pj_init` succeeds, then its control worker reports a startup failure. The actual worker explicitly handles failed thread registration, PJSUA creation, memory-pool/media initialization, ringback setup, UDP4 transport creation and PJSUA startup; all those paths complete with NO. No particular hardware/provider failure or timing frequency is assumed or reproduced.

[AKSIPUserAgent.start:319–329](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L319-L329) acquires the outer PJLIB reference and publishes Starting. Its completion sets Stopped on failure and posts DidFinishStarting, with no outer `pj_shutdown`. The [early thread-registration/create failure branches:341–355](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L341-L355) complete directly; [later failed initialization:440–447](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L440-L447), [UDP4 transport creation:497–504](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L497-L504) and [pjsua_start:570–575](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L570-L575) call `thread_stop` before the same failed completion. That [worker teardown:618–638](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L618-L638) releases the local pool and destroys PJSUA, but does not call the wrapper's outer shutdown. The only explicit wrapper release is [finishStopping:640–643](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L640-L643). Both [stop entry points:586–604](https://github.com/jpskidmore/telephone-jps/blob/9a32ae825e4d3bb380cb52b8452ddf7526764a25/Telephone/AKSIPUserAgent.m#L586-L604) return unless the state is Started, so the failure's Stopped state cannot reach that release. A whole-source search found no alternative wrapper balance.

**Exact SDK contract:** official 2.17 Unix [`pj_init`:204–214/256–263](https://github.com/pjsip/pjproject/blob/2.17/pjlib/src/pj/os_core_unix.c#L204-L263) counts each successful initialization, including calls made while already initialized. [`pj_shutdown`:281–317](https://github.com/pjsip/pjproject/blob/2.17/pjlib/src/pj/os_core_unix.c#L281-L317) decrements once and skips cleanup while references remain. Zero-reference cleanup runs registered exit callbacks and releases/reset the exception ID, critical-section/TLS and error handlers. PJSUA acquires a separate nested reference at [`pjsua_create`:966–968](https://github.com/pjsip/pjproject/blob/2.17/pjsip/src/pjsua-lib/pjsua_core.c#L966-L968). After successful creation, its [`destroy`:2209–2214](https://github.com/pjsip/pjproject/blob/2.17/pjsip/src/pjsua-lib/pjsua_core.c#L2209-L2214) releases that nested reference; it does not balance the app wrapper's additional successful initialization. Thus later native teardown cannot repair the missing outer release. This is a reference/resource-finalization defect, not evidence that every failure allocates another full resource set or that retries crash.

**Measured component evidence:** `StartupRefProbe.m` executes the existing Release `AKSIPUserAgent.start`, `stop`, `stopAndWait` and `finishStopping` implementations on initializer-free production-layout receivers. `pj_init` and `pj_shutdown` are scalar counter definitions that model the documented outer reference balance. Worker scheduling is an inert completion-result/stop recorder and never enters native worker code. All PJSIP/PJLIB archives are omitted; no SDK operation can be invoked by these tested paths. Actual nested PJSUA ref balance and retained native resources are source-traced, not measured.

All **36 assertions across six scenarios pass**. Rejected outer initialization keeps zero references and schedules no worker. A failed completion leaves Stopped, one outer reference and zero shutdown calls; both Stop entry points then schedule no teardown. Two failed completions leave two outer references. Successful synchronous and asynchronous stop controls each return to zero. Failure followed by a successful start/stop leaves the earlier one reference outstanding. Commands and source/original Release object hashes are in `provenance.json`, with scalar results in `results.json`.

No real endpoint/worker/network/provider/account/profile/defaults/credential/Keychain/Contacts, audio/device operation, application/agent/controller initializer, visible UI or OS setting was used. Local Foundation notifications have no application observers, and retained receivers exit without production cleanup. No native PJLIB reference count or allocation state was inspected.

**Future fix:** explicitly own the outer PJLIB initialization reference per startup attempt and release it exactly once after any failed worker teardown, on the appropriate owning thread. Keep native PJSUA cleanup and the wrapper reference separately balanced. Preserve successful stop behavior and startup-failure notifications; avoid publishing a spurious successful-stop transition or double-releasing when the initial `pj_init` itself failed.

**Regression expectations:** run released wrapper/worker-completion seams with reference recorders for failed thread registration, failed create/init/transport/start, repeated failure, failure followed by successful start/stop, initial PJLIB rejection and synchronous/asynchronous normal stop. All owned references must return to baseline after failure; cleanup must not run twice. Native resource/timing acceptance is a separate check.

**Deduplication:** reviewed #2–50, especially#25 activity-token cleanup after failed startup, #45 changed configuration during Starting and #50 premature codec enumeration. This is the unmatched native-library lifetime reference, independently measured at the wrapper's init/shutdown boundary. No application source was changed during the review.
